note: One entry per DEPLOY, newest first, timestamped in ET. Written for the trader, not for developers: each line says what he would NOTICE. The time matters - four deploys landed on 2026-08-31, so 'that day' cannot answer 'was that fix in the build I was running at 3pm?'. Add a new entry at the TOP each time something ships.

releases.heading: New GO + short RVOL + MACD filter
items: FILTERS > A/A+ Setup now offers GO + short RVOL + MACD (bull only). It requires GO, cyan RVOL on any of 5m/15m/30m, rising MACD above its signal on a completed 5-minute candle, and buyers in control on completed 30-minute candles.

Matching rows show a GO+ badge with the confirmation candle time in ET. The filter checks each refresh from 09:30 to 15:30 ET and removes rows when confirmation fades. Its RVOL/MACD checks are built in; the separate filter controls do not change them. This experimental setup does not guarantee a winning trade.

releases.heading: FILTERS now work the right way on the BEAR scanner
items: On BEAR, the SQZ and Skittles filters were still picking BULLISH signals (squeeze fired up, bullish crosses) - the opposite of a put scanner. Now one filter setting works on both: on BEAR each ticked colour means its down-side twin (SQZ fired up -> fired down; Skittles EMA/MACD crosses up -> the same crosses down), using the app's own bear rules.

On BEAR the panel shows the down-side colours and wording, the summary line says "bearish", the ⭐ star marks bearish crosses, and the History search's "buyers winning" becomes "sellers winning". BULL is unchanged. RVOL "bullish only", the strategy presets (GO/OPT/Best/V2/V3/Daily 2), grade and momentum already read the bear side.

releases.heading: Real RVOL: closing-auction and old readings are dimmed
items: RVOL numbers still match TOS exactly. But a reading that comes from the 3:50-4:10 PM closing auction (end-of-day fund orders - on Friday 55% of names lit up on the 4:00 candle) or from an earlier day now shows as a grey outlined box instead of bright cyan, and never pulses as live. Hover it to see why.

Tested first: changing the RVOL formula itself (market-hours-only or same-time-of-day) did NOT pick better stocks, and the opening readings actually help Daily 2 and MomoX A+ - so only the display changed.

releases.heading: Scanner links to your charts, like thinkorswim
items: A colour square now sits top-left in the MomX scanner - the same 9 link colours as your charts (Red, Yellow, Green...). Click any ticker in the scanner (Live or History) and the app jumps to Charts and puts that ticker in EVERY chart of that colour. Each chart keeps its own timeframe; charts of other colours do not change; saved layouts are never touched.
No chart of that colour on screen? The active chart takes it, so you always land on a chart showing the ticker. The option chain follows the ticker.

Works from the detached scanner window too: click there and the main window charts change. Each scanner window remembers its own colour (starts on Red). The lightning badge still opens the ticker card; your floating scanner windows and cards are still there when you come back.

releases.heading: MomX NEWS reads seven real sources, no guesswork
items: NEWS now pulls headlines from Yahoo Finance (search + RSS), Alpaca/Benzinga, Benzinga's own feed, Finviz, Nasdaq and SEC EDGAR filings - and a headline lands on a ticker only when the publisher itself tagged that ticker. Nothing is matched by guessing from the words.

Press NEWS: the sources are read again for the tickers on your board and a Headlines list opens above the table, grouped by ticker, newest first, each with the publisher, where it came from, the age and a one-line teaser. One line under the list says how many sources answered and names any that did not (e.g. "Unavailable: Finviz").

The News column keeps the MomoX3 look - the age plus a ✦ on every ticker that has a headline. The ✦ is green/red when the AI reader judged the story, otherwise tinted by the headline's own tone. Hover or tap it for the headline, publisher and link; the pop-up now also shows Fresh (under 24h) or Stored, the tone, and the teaser.
After every SCAN the news is refreshed in the background for the scanned tickers, so the column is current without pressing anything. The scan itself is never slowed or changed by news.
Older stored headlines (up to 7 days) now show as "Stored" instead of disappearing, so an empty News cell really means no publisher tagged the ticker this week.

releases.heading: Sector cards fold away
items: The HOT sector cards now have their own "v SECTORS" arrow above them: click to hide them, click again to show. Closed, one line still names every sector (🔥 for HOT), so nothing is hidden without a trace. Your choice is remembered.

releases.heading: MomoX A+: the High OI magnet is the stock's OWN biggest wall
items: No more fixed 1,000-contract minimum. The High OI piece now counts the stock's own biggest call wall above the price, within 2x the expected move - so a smaller stock like QMCO (35C, 739 contracts) counts. Hover the MX A+ tag to see the wall.
Still not back-tested (no open-interest history); the 4 PM scorecard tracks it.

releases.heading: Scanner shows only tickers that have options
items: The MomX scanner now scans ONLY tickers whose real option chain lists options - the same chain the ticker card uses, no hand-made list. Tickers with no options are not scanned at all (bull and bear). Next to TICKERS it says how many were left out, e.g. "11 no options" - hover to see which.

A new ticker (a new Mover, or one you type) is checked first - usually within a minute - and shows only if it has options. If the check cannot get an answer (Schwab down, still loading) the ticker waits as "checking"; it is never marked "no options" on a guess. Typing a ticker with no options now tells you so.

The W (weekly options) marker now comes from the real chains too: 328 of your 356 Watchlist tickers have weeklies. The old hand-made list was wrong for 157 of them (it missed 155 weekly names and wrongly marked MPC and NOC).
Movers: no-options names no longer take any of the 40 slots.

releases.heading: MomoX A+ now needs a High OI call wall
items: The MX A+ tag now also requires the fifth piece: a big call wall (1,000+ contracts) just above the price, within 2x the expected move - the same walls the ticker card shows. Hover the tag to see the strike, e.g. 750C (16,446 OI).

Only tickers already passing the other four pieces get their option chain checked, one every 15 seconds, so the scanner does not slow down. A tag can appear a minute later than before while the chain loads.
Open interest has no history, so this extra piece is NOT back-tested.

releases.heading: MomoX A+ tag
items: New violet-and-gold "MX A+ 09:35 W" tag in the Setup column: the competitor's A+ setup - news in the last 24h + RVOL cyan + a squeeze fire (2h, 4h, Daily or Weekly) + Skittles Daily, 2D, 3D, 4D, Weekly and Monthly all bullish (no ETFs). The first time it lines up today; W = the stock has weekly options. It lights the ⚡, flashes and pops a card like the other setups.

Back-test Sep 1-25: 39% hit +2% first, 35% hit -1.5% first, 37% ran +4% - the most of any rule tested; holding to the close did better than a tight stop. Not proven yet - the 4 PM scorecard now tracks it daily (with a held-to-close line).

releases.heading: ⚡ TODAY / NOW button, like MomoX3
items: The ⚡ filter is now one button, like ScannerX3: click to cycle ALL → ⚡ NOW → ⚡ TODAY. The number on it is how many names hold a live ⚡ right now. ⚡ TODAY = fired today and still in the upper half of its last hour; ⚡ NOW = passing the gates this second.

releases.heading: Scanner re-checks only the newest bars
items: Each scanner rebuild now re-uses the indicator values it already worked out and only recomputes the newest bars that changed - about 38% less work per rebuild. Checked on all 357 tickers: every value is identical to a full recompute.

releases.heading: Scanner refreshes sooner
items: The scanner used to rest for half as long as each rebuild took (up to 2 minutes) before starting the next one. It now rests about a fifth (at most 45 seconds), so new boards arrive sooner - the rebuild runs at the lowest computer priority, so your charts still come first.
Two internal speed-ups in how each ticker's timeframes are built (checked on 357 tickers: identical results).

releases.heading: LIVE ⚡ every second, like ScannerX3
items: The ⚡ next to a ticker is now LIVE: checked every second on the Schwab stream, not every 4 minutes. It lights when the stock passes the gates ($5+, last hour closed up, 4-hour volume above normal) and fires a signal (9x20, 4x8 or MACD cross, squeeze fire, or a volume spike on a green candle). Bright when fresh, fading over 2 hours, and it goes out the moment the price drops into the lower half of its last hour. Hover it to see what fired.
New ⚡ ALL / ⚡ TODAY / ⚡ NOW switch next to Scan matches only: TODAY shows the names whose ⚡ is on, NOW only those passing the gates this second.
New H/L⚡ sort: names at the top of an hour that really moved come first.
Tested against our own signals on 20 days: our GO and market-turn setups ran +4% two to four times as often as this ⚡ - use the ⚡ as a live watch light, not as the entry.

releases.heading: Scanner stays lean with the Five Pillars data
items: Behind the scenes: the checklist data is computed once per ticker instead of twice, and is left out of the History archive (History cards do not show the checklist), so the scanner and History do not get heavier.

releases.heading: Five Pillars checklist on every ticker card
items: Each ticker card now has a FIVE PILLARS box (the MomoX method): 01 Trend (EMA 9 > 21 > 50 on 30m), 02 Price action (squeeze on or fired up on 2h/4h), 03 Market structure (room left in today's expected move), 04 Sell target (nearest call wall, prior-day high, premarket high or psych level at least 1% above), 05 Buy signal (a 9x20 or MACD cross, a chart arrow or a squeeze fire in the last 30 minutes). Green ✅ / red ✖ per pillar and READY ✓ when all five agree. Being back-tested now - not proven yet.

releases.heading: ⚡ in the Setup column, like MomoX
items: An orange ⚡ now leads the Setup column when a GO, OPT, SOLO, TURN or 🔥 leader fired today, before the grade letter. It flashes for the first 10 minutes; hover it to see what fired.
The Explosive pattern icon changed from ⚡ to 💥, so ⚡ only ever means "a setup fired".

releases.heading: 🔥 HOT sectors survive a scanner restart
items: The morning's 🔥 HOT sectors are now saved to disk. Before, restarting the scanner (like today at 11:01) erased them, and a sector cannot turn 🔥 after 11:00 - so today's AI Data Centers and Defense flames were lost.

releases.heading: MomoX-style pop-up cards and flashing tickers
items: When a GO, OPT, SOLO, TURN or 🔥 leader fires, that ticker's card now pops up by itself (like the MomoX cards), with a flashing line "⚡ GO 09:40 · came 09:45 ET" and every signal on the ticker. Once per ticker per day, up to 3 at a time, on wide screens only. Turn it off with the new Pop-up cards box next to Scan matches only.
The ticker itself also flashes yellow in the Symbol column for the first 10 minutes after a setup fires.
Every ticker card (also when you click ⚡) now lists all of its signals on one ⚡ line.

releases.heading: Market turn alert + ⚠ 30m sellers warning
items: New: when SPY dips below its VWAP after 9:45 and then closes back above it (10:00-2:30), the scanner marks the 5 strongest names at that moment with a teal "TURN #1 11:05" tag and your phone gets one push. Strongest = above VWAP, up 1%+, 30-minute buyers in control (ADX 20+), no ETFs. 20-day test: 44% hit +2% first, 41% hit -1.5% first, 20% ran +4% - a small edge, not proven; the 4 PM scorecard now tracks it. Starts Monday (the scanner restarts after today's close).
New warning on setups: ⚠ 30m sellers - the 30-minute chart has sellers in control (-DI above +DI). In the test those entries won only 14-18% of the time.

releases.heading: 🔥 on the ticker too
items: Stocks listed in a HOT sector's box (its top 5 by % today) now carry a 🔥 right before the ticker in the Symbol column, e.g. 🔥BE, 🔥IONQ. Hover it to see its rank in the sector. Where money is going - not a tested buy signal on its own.

releases.heading: Moving-now sectors now show as 🔥 HOT
items: Sectors that used to show 🔸 moving now now show as 🔥 HOT - the sector box, its label and the industry name on each row. One name, one flame.
A leader's ▲vol now says which volume timeframe lit it, e.g. "ARQQ +3.2 ▲vol 1h" (RVOL on 15m, 30m or 1h at 1.0 or more).

releases.heading: Chart-arrow tags in lime
items: In the scanner's Setup column, the CALL2H / CALL4H / C2H / C4H tags that used to be yellow are now lime. The cyan ones stay cyan.

releases.heading: New tags in the Setup column flash
items: Anything new in the Setup column now flashes with a white ring for its first 10 minutes: GO, OPT, SOLO, 🔥 leader, SQZ fire and the chart arrows (CALL2H / CALL4H / C2H / C4H). The 10 minutes count from when the scanner first saw it, so a late-arriving arrow still gets its full flash.

releases.heading: Setups and filters back on, as before 9:30 this morning
items: FILTERS again offers Best setups, GO, OPT, SOLO, hot sectors and News + momentum, and the Setup column shows the ⭐ stars, GO, OPT, SOLO, 🔥 leaders, NEWS and ⚠ warnings again - exactly as this morning.
The new C2H / C4H and SQZ fire tags stay, and the columns (News, Event, frozen Industry / Symbol) are unchanged.

releases.heading: C2H / C4H arrows and SQZ fire in the Setup column
items: The Setup column now also shows the chart's short C2H / C4H arrows (like PYPL's C4H at 10:10 today) - only during market hours, 9:30 to 4:00, so the early-morning noise stays out.
New cyan-outline tag when the 2h or 4h squeeze fires, e.g. "SQZ 2h 10:07" (first fire of the day in market hours).
Both are shown so you can see them - they are not proven yet. A 30-day test is running; the Chart CALL2H / CALL4H filter still uses only the full CALL arrows.

releases.heading: Scanner back to yesterday: new setups switched off
items: The Setup column is back to how it was yesterday morning: your letter, ADX, CALL2H/CALL4H arrows and V2 / V3 / Daily 2 / G. The ⭐ stars, GO, OPT, SOLO, 🔥 hot-sector leaders, the NEWS setup tag and the ⚠ warnings are switched off.
FILTERS no longer offers Best setups, GO, OPT, SOLO, hot sectors or News + momentum; a saved Best setups choice now reads as Any. The industry boxes show plain participation again, without 🔥 / 🔸.
Kept as they are: the News and Event columns and the frozen Industry / Symbol columns. Everything switched off can be switched back on in one step.

releases.heading: Paused alerts no longer show on the chart
items: A paused alert (like "Paused @ Auto CALL OI 515.00") no longer draws a line or label on the chart. It is still in your Alerts list, where you can turn it back on.

releases.heading: Mag7 OI walls now read Schwab/TOS chains
items: The Mag7 OI walls board used Tradier, and your Tradier account is inactive, so it showed nothing. It now reads the option chains from Schwab/TOS (Tradier only as a backup). All 7 names load in about 2 seconds.

releases.heading: Premarket FEED card says BACKUP, not GAP
items: Your Tradier account is inactive, so the 4-7 AM candles come from the free Alpaca backup, about 15 minutes behind. The Premarket FEED card now says BACKUP (amber) instead of GAP / No data, because the candles are there - just a little late until about 7:15 AM.

releases.heading: Morning brief: SPY/QQQ and movers lines come back
items: On 9/24 and 9/25 the morning brief was missing the SPY/QQQ tape line and the gainers/losers lines. The server kept reusing a broken Schwab price connection that answered with nothing. Now an empty answer makes it reconnect on the next 5-minute build. Takes effect after the next backend restart.

releases.heading: Only Industry and Symbol stay frozen
items: When you swipe the scanner sideways, only Industry and Symbol stay on screen now. Time and Setup scroll with the rest. The order is still Industry, Symbol, Time, Setup.

releases.heading: Scanner columns: Industry | Symbol | Time frozen, then Setup
items: The column order is now Industry, Symbol, Time, Setup. When you swipe the board sideways, Industry, Symbol and Time stay on screen; Setup scrolls with the rest.
History uses the same order.

releases.heading: ⭐ order fixed: clean setups first
items: Inside the same group (GO or OPT), a setup with no ⚠ now gets the lower star number. Before, a GO with a ⚠ (like up 9% or fading) could be ⭐1 just because it came earlier.

releases.heading: News and Event columns, like MomoX
items: Two new columns next to % Chg. News shows how old the latest headline is (43m, 2h, 17h) - bright white when under 3 hours. A ✦ after it means the AI read the news: green = good news, red = bad news. Hover to read the headline.

Event shows the next earnings date (e.g. 11/2) with ☀ = before the open or ☾ = after the close. It turns amber when earnings are 7 days away or less - an option held through earnings can jump or get crushed.
Click either header to sort: newest news first, or nearest earnings first. You can move or hide them in Columns like any other column.

releases.heading: ⭐1, ⭐2 … on the best setups - no filter needed
items: You do not have to open FILTERS any more. On the normal scanner screen, the day's best setups (GO, or OPT seen before 10:00) now carry a gold ⭐1, ⭐2, ⭐3 … tag in the Setup column, in your tested order. ⭐1 is the top one by your rules. An amber ⚠ next to it means careful (a wrong-pick pattern like up big or fading).
Before 9:35 there are no stars - that is normal. No star all day = no setup that day.

releases.heading: Best setups is now ranked - best first, with ⚠ warnings
items: With ⭐ Best setups picked, the list is now in your tested order: GO inside a 🔥 hot or 🔸 moving-now sector first, then other GO, then OPT. Inside each group, cleaner names come first, then good news (NEWS ↑), then the earliest signal. Nothing else changed - same filter, same tags.

A setup that matches a wrong-pick pattern gets an amber ⚠ tag, e.g. '⚠ up 12% · fading': bad news (news ↓), already up 8%+, momentum fading, or price back under VWAP. Two or more warnings push it lower in the list.

releases.heading: FILTERS setup list is now grouped - one everyday choice on top
items: The A/A+ Setup dropdown is split into labelled sections: '⭐ Use every day' (Best setups - the only one you need), 'Letters only', 'Extra ideas (still being tested)', and 'My older strategies' (V2, V3, Daily 2, G, GO only, OPT only). Nothing was removed; it is just easier to find the one you use.

releases.heading: Fixed: 🔥 / 🔸 sector boxes printed their lines on top of each other

releases.heading: Hot sectors now start at 09:35, up to 2 a day
items: The 🔥 hot sector is now picked from 09:35 ET (after the first 5-minute candle), not 09:45, and up to 2 sectors a day can light - so a sector that starts moving later in the morning can still get the flame. In the back-test (checked every 5 minutes, Sept 1-23) this gave 45% wins and 25% losses for the sector's rising stocks, vs 27% / 47% starting at 09:45.

Honest correction: the single 🔥#1 stock lost about half the time in this more careful test. The group of rising stocks in the 🔥 box is the reliable part - pair it with GO / OPT rather than buying the #1 alone.

Thursday Sept 24 replayed through the new code: it would have lit Pharma (09:35) and Oil & Gas (09:40), which did not follow through, and missed Quantum / Space. SOLO would have caught TSSI at 09:45 (+5.3% more at the high).

releases.heading: Filter help text updated for the hot-sector choice
items: The explanation under 'Best setups in 🔥 hot sectors' now describes the current rule (one sector a day by a single score, 09:45-11:00) and says plainly that plain 'Best setups' is the tested everyday choice.

releases.heading: Sector first, then its stock: 🔥#1 / 🔥#2 tags
items: When today's 🔥 hot sector lights up (09:45-11:00 ET), its two strongest stocks at that moment get an orange tag like '🔥#1 Quantum' and '🔥#2 Quantum'. The picks stay fixed for the day.
FILTERS > A/A+ Setup has '🔥 Hot sector leaders (#1 / #2)'.

Back-test Sept 1-23: the hot sector's #1 at 09:45 won 50% and 36% ran +4% (avg upside +3.1%), vs 26% and 12% for a random stock in a moving sector. Only 14 hot sector-days - a small sample. Picking the day's single best stock early is not reliable (even the best method found it only about 1 time in 4).

releases.heading: New: SOLO tag - big money going into one stock
items: A bold magenta 'SOLO 9.8× vol' tag appears in the Setup column when, between 09:45 and 11:00 ET, a stock trades 5 to 20 times its normal volume for that time of day, is up 1% or more and holding above VWAP and the 09:30 price, costs $5 or more, and its sector is NOT moving with it - money aimed at that one company. It stays on for the day and shows when it fired.
FILTERS > A/A+ Setup has 'SOLO big-money stocks', heaviest volume first. The 4 PM scorecard has a SOLO line.

Back-test Sept 1-23: 57% ran +4% at some point (the most of anything tested), but about half gave the move back by the close. It is a fast mover: take profit into strength, do not hold all day. Checked on today's data: TSSI would have shown 'SOLO 9.8× vol' at 09:50 (+7.3%), closing +9.8%.

releases.heading: Hot sector: one combined score, one sector a day
items: The 🔥 hot sector is now picked by ONE score that mixes both signs of rotation - how much of the sector is up and above VWAP, and how fast its 3-day lead over SPY is growing - and the single strongest sector (at least half its stocks up) is marked between 09:45 and 11:00.
Back-test Sept 1-23: 45% wins, 27% losses, +0.55% average and 24% ran +4%, on 14 of 16 days - better than the two separate checks (43% / 37% / +0.35% / 16%) and it finds a sector on more days.

releases.heading: Sector boxes list their stocks and unusual volume
items: Each 🔥 / 🔸 sector box now lists the stocks to look at - the ones up and above VWAP, strongest first (e.g. 'PL +7.6 · IONQ +5.7 · RKLB +4.7'). A stock in cyan with '▲vol' also shows unusual volume right now (RVOL 15m, 30m or 1h at 1.0 or more).
The box also says how many of the group have unusual volume ('vol 4 of 6'). This volume count is shown only - it is not yet part of the hot rule until it is tested.

releases.heading: Sector rotation shows all day: 🔸 late rotation after 11:00
items: After 11:00 ET a sector that starts rotating is now shown too, with a 🔸 and a dashed amber box ('late · 3d +x% vs SPY'), and its stocks get a 🔸 on the industry name - so you see where money moves all day.
Only the 🔥 hot sectors (lit 09:45-11:00) feed the 'Best setups in 🔥 hot sectors' filter: in the back-test the late ones lost 17 of 17 as same-day trades. Treat 🔸 as a watch-list for the next morning.

releases.heading: New filter: Best setups in 🔥 hot sectors - and hot sectors only light 09:45-11:00
items: FILTERS > A/A+ Setup has 'Best setups in 🔥 hot sectors': only the GO / OPT tickers whose industry is a hot sector today.
A sector can now only TURN hot between 09:45 and 11:00 ET; once lit it stays lit for the rest of the day. In the back-test, sectors that only turned hot after 11:00 lost every time (0 wins in 17).
Why 3 days: of the windows tested (1, 2, 3 and 5 days vs SPY), 3 days gave the best result - 43% wins vs 31-33% for 1-2 days and 22% for 5 days.

releases.heading: Hot sectors show even when your filter hides their stocks
items: The 🔥 hot-sector boxes above the scanner table now always show, whatever FILTERS or 'Scan matches only' leaves on screen. Before, a filter that kept only a few rows also hid the hot sectors.

releases.heading: Sector rotation: hot sectors marked with a flame
items: The sector strip above the scanner now puts HOT sectors first with a flame and their 3-day lead over SPY, like '🔥 Quantum 6 of 6 ... 3d +3.9% vs SPY'. A sector is hot from 09:45 ET when its stocks beat SPY over the last 3 days, that lead is growing, and at least 60% of them are up and above VWAP. At most 2 a day.
Rows in a hot sector get a flame on their industry name, so a GO or OPT inside a hot sector stands out.

Back-test Sept 1-23: stocks in a hot sector won 43% of the time vs 26% elsewhere, but moved less (16% ran +4%). Treat it as a direction check, not a trade by itself - and do not chase the sector's biggest gainer, which did worse.

releases.heading: News first: the AI reads news on any ticker, and a 'News + momentum' filter
items: The AI news reader no longer waits for an A+/A letter. It reads any ticker whose headline is about that company alone and is fresh (since the evening before), newest first - A+/A tickers still go to the front of the line. Market round-ups ('10 stocks moving today') are skipped.

New choice in FILTERS > A/A+ Setup: 'News + momentum (AI news, then A/A+)'. It shows a ticker only when all three are true, in your order: the AI read the news as good (medium or high confidence), 5-minute momentum is Building or Extended, and the letter is A+ or A. Good news with no push never shows - that is not a trade.
Daily limit raised to 100 AI reads. Not back-tested yet: the AI reads start tomorrow, and the daily scorecard will show how it does.

releases.heading: New: AI news reader - a NEWS tag says WHY an A+/A ticker is moving
items: Each A+ or A ticker with fresh news now gets a small outlined tag in the Setup column, like 'NEWS Earnings ↑' (green), 'NEWS Offering ↓' (red) or 'NEWS Macro' (grey). Hover or tap it for the one-line reason, the headline it came from, and which AI read it. No tag means the headlines do not really explain the move.

Categories: Earnings, Upgrade, Downgrade, Contract, Product, FDA, Deal, Offering (the company selling new stock - usually bad), Legal, Macro. The arrow is about the NEWS, not the price: an offering is down-arrow even on a green day.
It uses Claude first. When the Claude credit runs out or Claude has a problem, it switches to the free Gemini by itself. Until a Claude key is added to the app it runs on Gemini.

To keep the credit safe it reads only A+/A tickers with news, once per new headline, from 06:30 to 15:30 ET on weekdays, and at most 60 reads a day. AI can be wrong - open the headline before trading on it.

releases.heading: CALL2H / CALL4H filter is back
items: FILTERS > A/A+ Setup has 'Chart CALL2H / CALL4H (live)' again: it shows every graded or scan-matched ticker with a live 2H or 4H arrow from the chart (2H arrows for 2 hours, 4H arrows for 4 hours), earliest first. It was removed by mistake when the strategy list was cut down to Best setups.

releases.heading: Best setups: GO first, and OPT only before 10:00
items: Best setups now lists GO tickers first, then OPT tickers - but an OPT only counts if it first shows before 10:00 ET. Once it shows, it stays on the list for the rest of the day, and the tag now reads 'OPT 09:40' (the time it first showed).

Why: Sept 1-24, OPT signals all day won 38% and lost as often as they won; GO plus OPT-before-10:00 won 55% (+0.52% a trade on the stock). Every OPT after 10:30 this week lost or went flat except one.
The OPT time is remembered in this browser: if you first open the app after 10:00, an earlier OPT will not show. Open the scanner before 10:00 on the device you trade from.

releases.heading: One choice instead of seven: Best setups
items: FILTERS > A/A+ Setup now offers only Any, A and up, A+ only and 'Best setups (GO or OPT)'. Best setups shows every ticker with a blue GO tag (gap and go) or a green OPT tag (turning up now) - the two setups that tested best.

Strategy V2, V3, Daily 2, G and Chart are gone from the dropdown, and their V2 / V3 / D2 / G tags no longer crowd the Setup column. The daily scorecard still checks them in the background. CALL2H / CALL4H arrow tags stay.
If you had one of the old strategies picked, it still shows as '(old)' until you change it.

releases.heading: New: GO tag for gap-and-go trades (the META Sept 21 picture)
items: A blue 'GO 09:45' tag shows in the Setup column when an A+ or A ticker gapped up 2% or more and, before 10:30, a 5-minute candle closed above VWAP, above the open and above the first 5-minute candle's high, with buyers in control on the 30-minute chart. The time is when that candle closed.
FILTERS > A/A+ Setup has a new choice, 'Gap and go (META Sep 21 picture)'.

Back-test Sept 1-23: 61 trades (about 4 a day), 44% ran +4% - the best of every setup tested so far (OPT 31%, all A+ 21%). Still a better list, not a sure win. Starts showing from the next market open.

releases.heading: New: Options setup (the META / MRNA picture)
items: A green OPT tag now shows first in the Setup column when a ticker looks like META and MRNA did this morning: A+ or A, a fresh Skittles cross on BOTH 2h and 4h, buyers in control on 30m (+DI above -DI) and momentum Extended. PLTR and INTC had the same A+ letter but none of these.
FILTERS > A/A+ Setup has a new choice, 'Options setup (META / MRNA picture)', to show only those tickers.

In the Sept 1-22 back-test this picture ran +4% (the size of move a cheap weekly call needs) 31% of the time, against 21% for all A+ and 15% for the PLTR / INTC picture. It is a better filter, not a sure thing - 35 trades is a small sample.

releases.heading: Both arrow colours now show: yellow 4/8 and cyan 9/20
items: The scanner used to fold a ticker's CALL2H / CALL4H arrows into one tag per label, so when both the 4/8 cross (yellow on the chart) and the 9/20 cross (cyan) fired, you only saw one. Each family now gets its own tag in the chart's colour: yellow = 4/8, cyan = 9/20. Example at 1:29 PM: FLY shows yellow CALL4H 13:00, cyan CALL4H 13:00 and cyan CALL2H 13:15.

releases.heading: CALL2H / CALL4H tags disappear when their candle is over
items: A CALL2H tag now stays on the scanner for 2 hours from its candle and a CALL4H tag for 4 hours - one candle of its own timeframe - then disappears. Before, a morning arrow stayed all day: WRBY still showed 'CALL2H 09:15' at 1:18 PM; it now went away at 11:15.
The FILTERS choice is now 'Chart CALL2H / CALL4H (live)' and follows the same rule, so it lists only tickers whose arrow is still current, earliest first.

releases.heading: Setup column: '5m cross' tag removed
items: The '5m cross 08:00' tag is gone from the Setup column - on the live board it sat on almost every row (even crosses from 4 AM premarket) and made the column hard to read. The Setup column now shows the letter, V2 / V3 / D2 / G, CALL2H / CALL4H, and ADX cyan.

releases.heading: FILTERS: the strategy count is right even before you press FILTERS
items: Picking Strategy V2 / V3 / Daily 2 / G / Chart CALL2H in the panel while the FILTERS button was still off showed the wrong number - e.g. '0 of 5 tickers - no ticker has qualified for V2' when 9 had - because the count only looked at the scan matches. The panel and the FILTERS button now count the same list the strategy shows.

Checked every choice tonight on yesterday's real lists, with FILTERS off and on: V2 9, V3 3, Daily 2 4 in #1-#4 order, G 1 with its option plan, Chart CALL2H/CALL4H 2 earliest first; A+ only / A and up / Any unchanged. With FILTERS off the board is still your normal scan matches.

releases.heading: Scanner: the ADX tag flashes when ADX has just crossed above 25
items: When a ticker's 5-minute ADX crosses up through 25 (the yellow line) on the latest bar with the cyan background, its 'ADX … cyan' tag in the Setup column turns solid cyan and flashes. On the next bar, if ADX stays above 25, it turns back to the steady outlined tag.
Like the steady tag, it only appears on tickers with a letter (A+ / A / B). Phones set to reduce motion get the solid colour without the blink.

releases.heading: Scanner: the Setup column is narrow again
items: The 'A/A+ Setup' column is now called 'Setup' and is about 40 px wide on the phone (it was about 150): its width was left over from when it printed words like 'Extended'. Tags (V2, D2 #1, CALL2H 13:00, ...) now wrap onto a second line instead of stretching the column.
The 'ADX … cyan' tag only appears on tickers that have a letter (A+ / A / B). Overnight almost every ticker sat in that state and the tag was noise on every row.

releases.heading: Scanner: the chart's ADX state ('ADX 32 cyan') on the row
items: The A/A+ Setup cell now shows 'ADX 32 cyan' when the 5-minute ADX pane on your chart would show the white ADX line above the yellow 25 line on a cyan background (+DI above 25) - the same calculation as the chart (Wilder, length 10).

It is shown as information, not used as a filter. Tested on Sept 1-22 with the chart's exact rule: V2 signals that were ALREADY in this state averaged +0.25% per trade, V2 signals that came BEFORE it averaged +1.01% - by the time ADX is strong with cyan the move has usually run. Best use: a sign the trend is healthy while you are in a trade, not a reason to enter late.
The 5 PM scorecard now also tracks 'Daily 2, ADX not strong yet' next to plain Daily 2, so live days can prove or disprove the early-entry idea.

releases.heading: A/A+ Setup column: no more 'Fading' - just the letter and your tags
items: The A/A+ Setup column no longer prints Fading / Holding / Extended / Building. That word only described the last few 5-minute candles, and 'A+ · Fading' read like a downtrend - FSLY showed 'A · Fading' at 1:00 PM on Sept 23, the very moment its chart fired CALL2H and CALL4H before a +25% run.
The column now shows only the letter (A+ / A / B, with the ⚡ or 📈 pattern icon) and your tags: V2, V3, D2 #1, G #1, CALL2H 13:00, 5m cross 10:50.
Nothing about the rules changed - V2 / V3 / Daily 2 still use the 5-minute reading behind the scenes, and clicking the letter still shows the full 'why' panel with it.

releases.heading: Chart: the A+ / A letter now shows where it appears; scanner shows the 5-minute arrow too
items: The chart now puts a green A+ or A bubble on the candle where the scanner's letter APPEARED, even when no CALL arrow fired there. Before, the letter only rode on arrows, so TSLA's A and FSLY's afternoon A+ on Sept 23 showed nothing on the chart. One bubble per letter per hour, so a letter that flickers on and off does not paint a row of bubbles.

The scanner's A/A+ Setup cell now also shows the chart's 5-minute arrow (EMA 9 crossing above EMA 20 - the CALL5 / C5 arrow) as '5m cross 10:50'. CRWD's green arrow before its Sept 23 run was this one.
The CALL2H / CALL4H tags now show only the full CALL arrows, not the small C2H / C4H (a cross against the bigger trend), which fired on many tickers in the early morning and buried the real ones.

releases.heading: Scanner: the chart's CALL2H / CALL4H arrows now show on the scanner
items: The scanner now runs the chart's own arrow calculator, so when your chart prints CALL2H or CALL4H, the scanner row shows the same arrow with its time, e.g. 'CALL2H 13:00' and 'CALL4H 13:00' in the A/A+ Setup cell (lime, like the chart's bubbles). Times are ET.

Why: on Sept 23 FSLY printed CALL2H + CALL4H at 13:00 ET on the chart and ran +25%, but the scanner's own columns (RVOL colours, A+) only lit up about 50 minutes later. Checked before switching on: FSLY 13:00 CALL2H/CALL4H and META 09:00 CALL2H come out identical on the scanner and the chart.
New choice in FILTERS > A/A+ Setup: 'Chart CALL2H / CALL4H today' - every graded or scan-matched ticker whose chart printed one of these arrows today, earliest first.

It is checked for the tickers that are graded (A+/A/B) or match the scan, about once a minute each, so it can appear up to about a minute after your chart - never the 50-minute gap. It starts from today; past days in History do not have it.

releases.heading: Strategy lists are no longer hidden by 'Scan matches only'
items: With 'Scan matches only' ticked, picking Strategy V2, V3, Daily 2 or G used to show only the tickers that were ALSO a scan match at that moment - so a G #1 or a Daily 2 entry that had dropped out of the scan simply disappeared. A picked strategy now always shows its whole day list (for example all 9 V2 tickers of Sept 23, not 4).

releases.heading: Scanner: Strategy G - your own entry rules, with the option plan and the real option result
items: FILTERS > A/A+ Setup now has 'Strategy G (my rules)'. It checks your method all day, 9:30 AM to 3:30 PM ET: RVOL cyan and rising on 30m or higher; SQZ on 2h and 4h fired or none; a 2h Skittles cyan cross today after 8 AM plus a 4h or Daily cross within 24 hours; the 5-minute price above the 20 EMA and VWAP, or a C5 / CALL5 arrow in the last 30 minutes.

Then the option check, the same way you read the chain: the target is the nearest 'C OI STRONG' call wall above the price, the contract is the chain's ENTRY call (delta closest under 0.20, nearest expiry after today), and the chain's ROI to the target must be 150% or more. A ticker only joins G when all of that passes.

Each G ticker shows 'G #1' and its plan in the A/A+ Setup cell, e.g. '→195 · 200C $0.68 · ROI 163%'. Checked against PLTR's chain on Sept 23: target 195, ENTRY 200C at $0.68, ROI 163% - the same numbers as your Options screen.

The app then re-prices that exact option every 5 minutes and applies your exit: sell when the stock reaches the target, sell if the option is down 50%, otherwise sell at 3:55 PM. The tag shows the result, and the 5 PM scorecard reports G's real option returns next to V2, V3 and Daily 2.
Option chains are only fetched for the few tickers that pass the first four rules (at most one chain every 15 seconds), so the app does not slow down.
A TEST, not proven: rules 1-4 averaged +0.43% per trade on the stock in the Sept 1-23 back-test; the option part has no history and is measured from tomorrow.

releases.heading: FILTERS: the top line no longer contradicts a picked strategy
items: With Strategy V2, V3 or Daily 2 picked, the line under ANY/ALL used to still say 'A ticker needs to pass just one switched-on group below'. It now says the strategy decides on its own and the dropdown and groups are not used until A/A+ Setup is set back.

releases.heading: Strategy V2 / V3 / Daily 2: judged at the signal, the way they were tested
items: A ticker is now judged ONCE - at the moment its first A or A+ of the day fires - and if it passes it stays on that day's list. This is exactly how the back-test and the 5 PM scorecard measure the rules.

Why: checking the rules on every refresh was replayed on Sept 22 and put 21 tickers on Daily 2 by 10:02 AM, with HOOD as #1 at 9:35 (its A+ fired at 9:34). In the first minutes RVOL reads high on most of the board, so the list flooded. That was not the tested rule.
Replaying Sept 22's real signals through the new version gives V2 = 15 tickers, V3 = 9, and Daily 2 #1 GOOGL (9:35), #2 MDB (9:43) - the same answer the scorecard gives.

The trade-off: a ticker whose first signal failed (e.g. momentum Fading at that moment) does not qualify later that day just because momentum turns - unless it later gets a NEW letter (its first A+ after an A).

releases.heading: Scanner: Strategy V2, V3 and Daily 2 - one choice instead of reading every column
items: FILTERS > A/A+ Setup now also offers Strategy V2, Strategy V3 and Strategy Daily 2. Pick one and it is the whole filter - the app checks every rule for you.
V2 = A+ or A, from 9:35 AM ET, up less than 10% today, momentum Extended, RVOL push. V3 = V2 plus a squeeze fired (4h/D/Wk). Daily 2 = V2 with RVOL on 2 or more timeframes.

Daily 2 numbers the tickers #1, #2, #3 in the order they qualified today and lists them in that order. A ticker stays on the Daily 2 list after it qualifies, even if its momentum turns later - the list is the day's entries. It does not stop at 2.
The A/A+ Setup column on the board now shows a small V2, V3 or 'D2 #1' tag beside the grade, whatever the filter is set to.
While a strategy is picked, RVOL, SQZ, SKITTLES, Momentum and Pattern are greyed out and left out. Your own settings in them are kept for when you switch back.

These rules are a TEST, not proven. In the 15-day back-test Daily 2 averaged +1.07% per trade (sell at +2%, cut at -1.5%), but on the first live day (Sept 22) its two picks both hit the -1.5% stop. The 5 PM scorecard compares V2, V3, Daily 2 and plain A+ every day.

releases.heading: FILTERS: a blank RVOL reading no longer counts as 0.00
items: Clearing the RVOL threshold box in FILTERS used to save 0 the instant the box went empty - and the box IS empty for a keystroke every time you clear 2.5 to type 1.5. So the filter could quietly drop to 'any reading at all' while you were still typing. The box now keeps the number that was already there until a new one is typed.

With a threshold sitting at 0, a timeframe whose RVOL had no reading yet - a study that has not warmed up - was read as 0.00 and PASSED. Those tickers reached the board with nothing behind them. A blank reading now fails the filter instead of counting as zero.
Worth knowing how common that is: 2,662 blank RVOL readings sit in the saved Watchlist history, and 1,780 of them are on 4h - which is ticked by default.
A genuine 0.00 reading is still a reading, and still passes a threshold of 0. Only 'no reading at all' is turned away.
History FIND already treated a blank reading this way, so the board and the history never disagreed. It now has a test holding that in place, so a later change cannot quietly pull the two apart.

releases.heading: Startup after a reboot: no more needless restart of the data server
items: After the computer restarts, the data server's first start can take more than 3 minutes. The background keeper gave it only 3 minutes before deciding it was stuck and starting it over, which added about 2-3 minutes to every reboot (seen 2026-09-22 at 11:10 PM).
It now allows 5 minutes. A slow first start after a reboot finishes on its own instead of being thrown away. A server that is really stuck is still replaced, just a bit later.
Takes effect the next time the computer restarts - nothing running now was touched.

releases.heading: Chart: signal ARROWS now carry the A+/A/B letter too
items: THIS is why the letters looked missing on the phone. The grade was only ever drawn by the bubble renderer. A chart profile that shows the 9x20 signals as ARROWS instead of bubbles - which is how the phone is set up, while the desktop shows bubbles - got no letter at all. Same code, different saved chart settings per device, so the desktop had letters and the phone had none.

The letter now rides the signal, not one way of drawing it: an arrow shows A+, A or B above it. It only appears when no bubble is drawn for that same signal, so a chart showing both does not print the letter twice.

Checked against real data before shipping: GOOGL's four morning Call signals on 2026-09-22 (CALL1H and CALL30 at 09:00, C15 at 09:15, CALL30 at 09:30) all now show 'A' on the arrow, and SPY's 10:00 C15 shows 'A+'.
The faded / struck-through style for an underwater signal is still bubble-only - an arrow is too small to strike through legibly.

releases.heading: Chart header badge: a ticker with no grade now shows a dash, not nothing
items: The grade badge in the chart header now always draws. A ticker with a letter shows it (META - 5m A); a ticker without one shows a muted dash (SPY - 5m -), with the tooltip 'No scanner setup grade right now'.

The first version drew nothing when there was no letter, which was a mistake: 'this ticker has no setup' and 'the badge did not load' looked exactly the same. GOOGL after hours is correctly ungraded - so is most of the board, 320 of 358 rows - and a blank header read as the feature being broken.

releases.heading: Chart header now shows the scanner's letter - readable on a phone
items: The chart header now carries the scanner's CURRENT setup letter next to the ticker and timeframe: GOOGL - 5m (A+). Always in the same place, so you never have to hunt for it.

Why: the letter circles sit on the Call bubbles, and on a phone those can all be crowded into the left edge of the screen. GOOGL on 2026-09-22 is the case - all four of its Call signals fired between 09:00 and 09:30 and stacked behind a PUT bubble at the very edge; everything after was PUTs, which never carry a letter. It read as 'the letters are missing on mobile' when they were simply off the side of the screen.
The two are different on purpose: the badge is what the scanner says RIGHT NOW, the circles are what it said at the moment each signal fired. The circles never change.
No badge appears when the ticker has no letter, which is the normal state for most of the board. Several chart panels on one ticker share a single request a minute between them.

releases.heading: Chart: a signal that is now underwater is faded and struck through
items: The A+/A/B circle beside a Call bubble now fades and gets a line through it when price is BELOW where that signal fired. GOOGL today is the case that asked for it: its 09:35 A+ was correct when stamped - 7 of 8 timeframes bullish, price climbing 357 to 363 - and then gave the whole day back to close at 352. The circle used to look just as alive at 16:00 as it did at 09:35.

The letter itself is never changed. What the scanner saw at that second stays on the chart forever; only the circle's appearance says whether it is still working. A grade that rewrote itself later would make every past signal look smarter than it was.

The mark means one thing with no hidden threshold: price is now below the price when the signal fired. Two other rules were measured first and thrown out - 'closed below the 30-minute trigger' fired on 94.5% of today's 4,026 graded signals and 'two closes below it' on 89.9%. A mark on 19 circles out of 20 tells you nothing. This one lands on about 43%.
A dip that recovers does not count - the mark follows the latest bar, so a signal that goes underwater and comes back becomes solid again.

releases.heading: Scanner grade: a MACD cross against the trend no longer counts as bullish
items: The grade counted a timeframe as bullish when MACD crossed up EVEN IF the 9 EMA was still below the 20 EMA - a cross against the trend. On the chart that cell is painted dark green with a DOWNTICK marker, so the chart was already calling it bearish while the grade scored it bullish. QCOM is the clearest case: its 4h cell read 23 with a downtick, and that single cell was what made it a B.
Now every bullish cross the grade counts must be confirmed by the 9 EMA being above the 20 EMA - which is what cyan, green and lime already required. Only dark green did not.

What changes on your board: fewer letters, and the ones left are cleaner. Measured across the whole 23-day archive (204,075 snapshots): A+ down 12%, A down 21%, B down 23%; about 1 snapshot in 20 changes letter. Nothing is re-ranked - the gate just got honest.

In the back-test over the same archive, A+ went from 45.7% to 46.8% closing higher and the ladder now runs in the right order (A+ 46.8% > A 43.6% > B 42.9%); before the fix B was beating A. That is a small gain on 310 signals and is NOT proof of an edge - the grade still has none worth trading on its own.

releases.heading: Ticker card: the nearest high-OI wall each side, in expected moves
items: Strike reach on the lightning card now ends with NEAREST WALL EACH SIDE: the closest call wall above the price and the closest put wall at or below it, each with its open interest, its expiry, how many dollars away it is, and what that is as a multiple of the expected move. On NEM at $127.90 it reads: up 129C 455 OI Fri 9/25 +$1.10 = 0.26x, down 125P 2k OI Fri 10/16 -$2.90 = 0.22x.

NEAREST, not biggest. NEM's heaviest call wall is 135C and its heaviest put 120P, but the strike the price has to get through first is 129C - that is the one shown. The walls block directly above still lists the big ones.

Each wall is measured against its OWN expiry's expected move. A monthly wall judged by this Friday's move would look far closer than it is. When the chain has no move for the wall's expiry, the line borrows the nearest one and names it, rather than mixing the two silently.
Colour is the same scale as the strike checker: green inside 1x, amber 1-2x, red beyond 2x.

releases.heading: Chart: the A+/A circle now shows on far more CALL bubbles
items: The green A+/A circle beside a CALL bubble was missing on most signals. The chart only showed it when the scanner happened to record a grade INSIDE that exact candle - but the scanner records roughly every 8 minutes (measured today: median 8.1 min, worst 28), while a 5-minute candle is only 5 minutes wide. So most CALL bubbles came up bare even when the scanner had graded the ticker A+ all morning, which is exactly what happened on META today.

A CALL bubble now uses the most recent grade recorded at or before its candle, reaching back up to 15 minutes - the grade that was actually live when the signal fired. A reading older than that is left off rather than shown, and a grade recorded later is never pulled backwards onto an earlier candle.
Unchanged: the circle still only appears on bullish CALL bubbles. Fire bubbles and PUT bubbles carry no grade.

releases.heading: Scanner now records ADX (trend strength)
items: The scanner now reads the same ADX study your chart draws - ADX(10, WILDERS) with +DI and -DI - on every ticker's 5-minute and 30-minute bars, and writes it down. The numbers match the chart exactly (checked bar for bar against the chart's own code on INOD and NVDA).
Your A+/A/B grade has NOT changed. ADX is recorded alongside it, not folded into it. Nothing you see in the Setup column, the filters, or the alerts is graded any differently than yesterday.

Why: INOD ran 11.9% from 13:42 on Monday and the scanner only ever graded it B. On the chart, ADX turned up from 12 to 35 at 13:45 as +DI crossed -DI (48.6 against 13.0) - the earliest clear tell there was. Recording it is how we find out whether that cross is worth trading, instead of guessing.
The Fresh column has a new ADX mark. When +DI crosses -DI it logs a line like "ADX 5m bull cross (ADX 35 up)", once per cross - not once per scan.
The Setup "why" panel has a new "Trend strength (ADX)" block showing +DI, -DI and ADX for 5m and 30m, with an arrow when ADX is rising.

Every grade and pattern the scanner records now also stores which part of the day it happened in - Premarket, First 30m (Smart), Morning, Midday, Second 30m (Smart), Power Hour or After hours - using the same session lines your chart draws. So in a few weeks the track record can answer "does this work in the Second 30m?" rather than only "does this work".

The track record gained three new cuts: by session window, and by whether a +DI cross (with or without ADX rising) was in place when the signal fired. They will read as empty until enough days have been recorded.

Three fixes to the above before it went live: reading ADX no longer slows the scan (it was adding about eight seconds to every full watchlist pass, and now adds none); a cross on the bar still forming can no longer be written to the Fresh timeline twice as the candle moves around - one cross, one line, and a genuine new cross on the next bar still shows; and History no longer stores the ADX numbers on every saved row, which was growing the day's file by about 15% for a reading already kept on each recorded grade. History's "why" panel now says "No ADX reading saved for this History row" instead of showing an empty block.

releases.heading: Charts and scanner are fast again
items: Charts, ticker cards and the scanner went slow this afternoon - a card that normally opens in seconds took three to four minutes. Fixed at the root.

What was happening: when a chart's background refresh looked stuck, the app started a fresh one but never stopped the old one. The abandoned copies kept piling up in line and still did the full work when their turn came, so the server spent its time rebuilding charts nobody was waiting for.
Abandoned refreshes are now thrown away the moment they come up, instead of being rebuilt.
A refresh that is simply waiting its turn is no longer mistaken for a stuck one, so the app stops creating duplicates of work already in progress.
Deep chart rebuilds (the slow, full-history kind) now run in their own lane, so they cannot crowd out the quick refresh that keeps today's candles current.
No change to what you see on a chart: same candles, same studies, same labels - they just arrive on time again.

releases.heading: Ticker card: Strike reach
items: The ⚡ ticker card has a new Strike reach block under the High-OI walls. For the next three expiries it shows the expected move in dollars and percent, and how far calls and puts sit at 1× and 2× that move from the live price.

Type a strike into "Check a strike" (for example 160C Fri, 95P 9/25, or just 160) to see the move it needs by expiry and how many expected moves that is. Green means inside 1×, amber is 1–2×, red is more than 2×. A strike already in the money says so.

It measures from the scanner's live price, not the option chain's older snapshot price, and shows when the chain was captured. If the chain is more than 15 minutes old, an amber line warns that the expected moves may be out of date.
If you type a weekday the ticker has no expiry on (like Thu on a Friday-only name), it tells you which expiries are listed instead of guessing.
Expected move is the size of move today's option prices are paying for by that expiry - it is not a forecast and not a recommendation.

Fixed a round of rough edges: the 1x/2x color now rounds before it decides (a strike sitting at exactly 1x, like 155C on a $147.60 stock with a $7.40 move, no longer flashes amber by a fraction of a cent), and the box now reads a symbol or weekday out front too ("SHOP 160C Fri", "Fri 160C"). A bare strike now defaults to the nearest expiry that actually has an expected move, and today's own expiry drops off the list after 4pm ET. The warning line is clearer too: it says when the chain's capture time is unknown, when the server marked it stale but it's still fresh, or when the chain simply failed to load (with a nudge to reopen the card).

Setup "why" panel: every timeline line now shows both times - the bar the change belongs to and the moment the scanner saw it, e.g. "RVOL 5m 2.1 · bar 13:40 · seen 13:53". A squeeze release or a multi-day Skittles colour can be hours older than the line that reported it. When the bar time is not known, only the seen time is shown.

releases.heading: Scanner columns: drag with the mouse, right-click to hide
items: Grab any column header on the scanner (Live and History) and drag it left or right. A cyan line shows where it will land; let go and it stays there, saved on this device.
Right-click any column header for a small menu: Hide column, Move left, Move right, or Show all columns (brings back everything you hid, keeps your order).
Dragging never re-sorts the board - a plain click on a header still sorts like before. Press Esc mid-drag, or let go off the headers, to cancel.
Symbol can be moved but not hidden. Hidden columns stay listed in the Columns button so you can tick them back on, and the RVOL / SQZ / SKIT group labels follow the new order.
A quick flick-and-release drag now always moves the column. Before, letting go the instant you crossed onto a new header could leave the column where it was.

Symbol, Setup and Time are now frozen on the left of the scanner (Live and History) on every screen, phone included: swipe sideways and they stay put while Fresh and everything else scroll. On Live, Time now sits right after Setup. Drag Setup away (or hide it) and it scrolls like any other column. Also: the cyan drop line now shows exactly where the column lands next to the Time column, and dropping a header onto a text box no longer types anything into it.

On a phone the frozen Symbol + Setup + Time block is much narrower (about 57% of the screen instead of 79%): Setup shows its grade on top and the momentum word underneath, and Symbol drops its small time stamp because the frozen Time column right beside it shows the same time. The last frozen column now has a clearer edge so you can see where the sliding part starts.
The cyan drop line now shows on the last frozen header too (Time on Live, Setup on History). Before, dragging a column onto that header showed no line even though the column still landed there.
The grade column is now called "A/A+ Setup", so it is clear where the A+ / A / B letter is.

releases.heading: FILTERS: a switched-off group now looks switched off
releases.subheading: And a line under ANY / ALL says exactly what the filter is using
items: A group whose own box is unticked (RVOL, SQZ or SKITTLES) is now greyed out, with a dashed border and OFF next to its name. Its timeframes can stay ticked - they do not count until you tick the group's own box.

Under the ANY / ALL dropdown a new line says what the filter is really using, for example: 'In the filter: SKITTLES. Left out (off): RVOL and SQZ.' A group that is on but has no timeframe ticked is listed as left out too, and any Setup / Momentum / Pattern filter you set is named with the groups.

Why: this morning ALL showed 15 tickers without any RVOL. On your phone RVOL's own box was unticked, but 1h/2h/4h were still ticked inside it, so it looked on. The filter did what the boxes said - the panel just made it easy to misread.
The Skittles star switch works whether or not SKITTLES is filtering, so it stays bright when the rest of an OFF Skittles group is greyed.
Same on the PC and on the phone. The greyed boxes still work - you can set a group up first and switch it on after.

releases.heading: Scanner grade (experimental): A+/A/B, momentum and pattern
releases.subheading: New Setup and Fresh columns, a Columns button, and grade circles on the chart
items: Setup column: the scanner grade (A+ / A / B), the move's pattern (⚡ Explosive or 📈 Steady) and its momentum right now (Building ↑, Holding, Fading ↓, Extended). Example: "A+ ⚡ · Building ↑". Moves without a letter but with a pattern show as "– 📈 · Building ↑" (like NFLX on Sept 21).
Fresh column: what changed in the last 15 minutes and when (e.g. "SKIT 4h 09:32 · RVOL 5m 09:33 · 2m").
Click a Setup cell to see exactly why it qualified: SKIT timeframes, volume and news (shown separately), squeeze, position in the range, momentum, and today's timeline.
FILTERS: new Setup (A and up / A+ only), Momentum (Building only) and Pattern choices. They work together with the ANY / ALL setting.
Columns button: move columns left or right, hide or show them, or reset. Saved on this device.
Chart: A+/A/B circles next to bullish CALL labels on Watchlist and Mag7 tickers, using the grade recorded during that candle. Circles start appearing from today's recording onward.

Track record: every first A+/A/B of the day and every Steady/Explosive move (09:30-16:00 ET) is recorded and scored each evening (15 min, 1 hour, close, best and worst move). Until recorded results exist it shows the back-test: A+ 334 signals over 14 trading days, 44% closed higher.
A+ means the defined conditions align. It is not a recommendation and does not guarantee profit.

releases.heading: FILTERS: ANY or ALL of the groups - your choice
releases.subheading: Pick ALL to keep only tickers that pass every group you switched on
items: New dropdown at the top of the FILTERS panel: ANY of the following / ALL of the following - the same choice as the top of a TOS scan. Each group keeps its own dropdown for its timeframes.

ALL: a ticker stays on the board only if it passes EVERY group you switched on. Example: RVOL on + SKITTLES on + ALL = only tickers with an RVOL hit AND a bullish Skittles cross. A group you switch off (like SQZ) is left out - it does not block anything.
ANY is still how it starts, so your board looks the same until you pick ALL. Your saved filter settings were kept - nothing was reset. Your ANY/ALL choice is remembered like the rest of them.
The FILTERS button on the toolbar is still the on/off switch - it lights up purple while the board is filtered. The panel's 'N of M tickers' shows what you will get.
If the filter leaves 0 tickers, the panel now says which group passed nobody - for example 'RVOL passes no ticker right now - and ALL needs every switched-on group to pass.'

Wording fix: when Skittles passed nobody, the panel's note talked only about a 'cyan' Skittles. It now talks about the Skittles crosses you ticked - by default the four bullish ones (EMA 9/20 up, MACD up with 9 over 20, EMA 4/8 up, MACD up).

'Bullish only' now says what it really checks. It said 'green or cyan block', but under 2.0 there is no block - only the number's colour. The reading must be green or cyan (the bar closed in the top half of its range); a red or magenta reading never counts, whatever the number. That is why CVS did not pass tonight: its daily RVOL read 0.8, in red.

releases.heading: AI and security stocks now have their own industries
releases.subheading: 26 tickers regrouped using your Sector ETFs sheet
items: AI - Data Centers: CRWV, NBIS, APLD, SMCI, DELL, HPE, VRT, ORCL (were AI-Infra, Tech-HW or Software).
AI - Networking: ALAB, CRDO, ANET, CIEN, CLS, RMBS (were Semis, Networking or Tech-HW).
AI - Power: CEG, VST, TLN, GEV (were Utilities). AI - Cloud: SNOW, MDB, DDOG (were IT Services or Software).
Cybersecurity: CRWD, PANW, ZS, NET (were Software). UMAC moves to Drones.

Nothing else changed: AVGO, NVDA and the other chip makers stay Semis, and COIN and MSTR stay Capital Markets. When these AI names move together they now show as one group in the 'which sector is moving' line.
Old History days keep the industry they were saved with.

releases.heading: History scrolling no longer lags
releases.subheading: Every thumb swipe was rebuilding the whole page behind the scenes
items: What was wrong: the scanner watched every scroll movement to decide whether to show the TOP button, and each movement made the whole scanner redraw - and with it the full History table (up to 400 rows). Measured on a phone-speed test: one swipe caused four redraws of the scanner and three full rebuilds of the table, each a 100-270 ms freeze. Now the scroll is only noticed when the answer changes (top vs not top), and the table is left alone unless its own data changed.
The History table also no longer rebuilds on every live-board refresh tick while you are on it.

TOP button now appears on the History tab too. It was only ever wired to the live board, so the 400-row page - where you most need a way back up - never had one. Scroll down and it appears; tap it and you are at the top.
After the fix the same phone-speed test shows no scanner redraws during a swipe; what remains is the browser painting a big table, which is normal.

releases.heading: History search: Day, Time and Ticker - alone or all three together
releases.subheading: Typing a time on the iPhone now works; the date is a picker, not just arrows
items: Why 09:30 was 'not taking' on your phone: the box already held a full time and the tap put a cursor next to it instead of selecting it, so the box was full and every digit you pressed was thrown away. And the number pad has no Enter or colon key, so there was no way to type 09:30 and no way to run it. Now the box empties the moment you tap it, the time you had is shown as a grey hint, and typing 0930 turns into 09:30 by itself.
A Go button sits next to the Time box. Closing the keypad also runs the jump, because that is the one exit every phone has.
The date is now a real picker: tap the day and the phone's wheel opens listing only the days that are actually in the archive. The arrows still step one day.

Any combination works. Day alone shows that day. Time alone jumps within the day on screen. Ticker alone searches all days. Day + Ticker shows that ticker on that day only. Day + Time scrolls that day to that time. Ticker + Time scrolls the ticker's entries to the first one at or after that time. All three: that ticker, that day, that time.
When a ticker is typed, the day picker gains an 'All days' choice at the top - that is the old behaviour, and it is what you get until you pick a day.

A time it cannot read is now said in words next to the box ('Enter a time like 09:45') instead of a hidden tooltip the phone never showed. A jump hidden by the NEWS filter says so too, rather than doing nothing.
The count beside the date is the day's real total (11770 entries on Friday), not the 400 on the page.

Checked on an iPhone-sized screen against the live archive: 0930 typed digit by digit reads 09:30; Go flashes 10:32 on today; Friday 0945 pages to 'showing 799-1198' with 09:45 highlighted; AAL + Friday + 10:00 lands on AAL's 10:01 row; 'All days' brings back AAL across three days.
Day + Ticker needs the scanner restarted to narrow to one day - double-click 'Restart MomX Scanner.bat'. Until then a ticker search still shows all days.

releases.heading: Jump to a time now visibly moves - it scrolls to the row and flashes it
releases.subheading: On today's short day there was no page to move to, so it looked broken
items: You typed 0930 and nothing happened. Here is why: today has 46 entries and a page holds 400, so the whole day was already on screen - there was no page to move to, and paging was the only thing the jump did.
It now always shows you where it went. It jumps the page when the page needs to move, and then scrolls the row into view and flashes it cyan for a couple of seconds. On a short day it just scrolls.

Second thing you would have hit: there is no 09:30 entry on today at all - the session bar shows no Open count. It lands on the next moment that WAS recorded (10:32 today) and the box repaints to that time, so you can see it moved rather than being told 'nothing found'.
Checked on both kinds of day: on today it scrolls to and flashes 10:32; on Friday, typing 0945 moves the page from 'showing 11371-11770' to 'showing 799-1198' with 09:45 at the top, highlighted.
Reload to pick it up.

releases.heading: FIND is live. Reload the page and it works.
releases.subheading: The reason it kept returning nothing was a one-word bug of mine, not the restart
items: It works now: RVOL 1h over 3 with buyers winning returns 137 tickers over 6 days - BILI, ALAB, HUT, USAR, DRAM and the rest, each with when it first hit, when it last hit, how many times and its peak reading. Checked through the exact path your phone uses.

What was actually wrong: I named a variable in the scanner the same as the piece of code that does the searching, so the search crashed on every request. The restart was necessary but was never going to be enough on its own. That was my mistake and it cost you three rounds of asking.

Six other things were found and fixed in the same pass, before you hit any of them: the Jump-to box could not be typed into (it was pre-filled to its character limit so your keystrokes were dropped), FIND's 'this day' was quietly searching every day instead, clicking a ticker in the results did nothing, a search run while the scanner was starting up said 'no archive at all', switching lists left the old results on screen, and closing the box left a stale error behind.

The Jump-to box works too: type 0945 on the History tab and press Enter. The session line reads Pre 607, Open 479, Morning 3344, Midday 4322, Power 1525, After 1473 for Thursday - click any of them to jump there.
Reload the page on your phone to pick it up. The scanner rebuilt its boards during the restart and is back to normal.

releases.heading: Double-click "Restart MomX Scanner" and FIND starts working
releases.subheading: Proved the whole thing works first - here is exactly what you will see
items: There is now a 'Restart MomX Scanner.bat' in your project folder, next to 'Start Trading App.bat'. Double-click it. The PowerShell script alone may have silently refused to run - this machine blocks unsigned scripts, which is probably why nothing happened.

Before asking you to run it again, I proved the whole chain works. I ran the new code on a spare port and drove your actual app against it: FIND returned '137 tickers over 6 days' for RVOL 1h over 3, with BILI, ALAB, HUT, USAR, DRAM, MP and the rest listed with their first hit, last hit, how many times and peak reading. The Jump box and the session line both appeared.
So the only thing standing between you and that screen is the scanner worker still running Friday afternoon's code.
The restart takes about 15 seconds, then a couple of minutes for the boards to fill back in. The script checks FIND actually answers afterwards and tells you - it does not just claim success.
Nothing else is affected while you wait.

releases.heading: FIND told you nothing when it failed - now it tells you exactly what to do
releases.subheading: You pressed Search and saw no result. It had failed, and the message was hidden behind the box.
items: The error was being drawn on the page UNDERNEATH the FIND window, so from where you were looking the Search button simply did nothing. That was my mistake. The message now appears inside the FIND box, right above the Search button.
And it says something you can act on. Instead of 'Not Found' it now reads: 'The scanner worker has not picked up this feature yet - it needs restarting once. Everything else keeps working meanwhile.'
That is exactly what is happening. The scanner worker is still running Friday afternoon's code, so FIND has nothing to talk to and the Jump-to time box cannot appear either.

To fix it there is now a script: scripts/restart-momx-worker.ps1. Right-click it and Run with PowerShell. It stops the worker, waits for it to come back, and then actually checks that FIND answers - so it tells you it worked rather than just claiming it.
Nothing else is affected while you wait. The live board, the alerts and the rest of History all keep working.

releases.heading: Jump to a time on the History tab
releases.subheading: Plus a line showing how busy each part of the day was, before you click into it
items: A small 'Jump to' box sits next to the ticker search. It is never empty - it always shows the time the page you are looking at starts at, so the format is sitting right there. Type 945, 9:45 or 09:45, press Enter, and History jumps to that moment and runs forward.

If nothing was recorded at exactly that time, it lands on the next moment that was and the box repaints to show you the time you actually got. Quiet stretches stay visible instead of reading as 'nothing found'.
A line above the table shows the whole day at a glance. For Thursday Sep 4 it reads: Pre 607, Open 479, Morning 3344, Midday 4322, Power 1525, After 1473. Click any name to jump straight there.

It MOVES the page, it does not filter. Nothing is hidden - the entry count, Newer/Older and NEWS all keep meaning exactly what they mean today. That matters because a day holds about 11,770 entries and a page holds 400; a filter would have had to either search a fraction of the day or redefine every counter on that bar.
A time it cannot read outlines the box amber and says 'Enter a time like 09:45' rather than jumping somewhere you did not ask for.
Like FIND, this needs the scanner worker restarted once - the times it jumps between come from new code the running worker has not picked up.

releases.heading: FIND needs one backend restart before it can answer
releases.subheading: The button and the search box are live; the part that reads the archive is not running yet
items: The FIND button is on the History bar now and the search box works - pick a column, a timeframe, a number or the colours, and it tells you exactly what it will search.
Pressing Search will show an error until the scanner worker is restarted, because the piece that reads the archive is new code the running worker has not picked up. I could not restart it from here.
Restart it whenever suits you - it is a background service, and it rebuilds the boards on its own afterwards. Nothing is lost by waiting.

releases.heading: FIND - search the whole archive for tickers that hit a condition
releases.subheading: New button on the History bar. "Which tickers had 1h RVOL over 3?" - answered across 30 days.
items: Press FIND on the History tab, pick a column (RVOL, SQZ or SKITTLES), a timeframe, and either a number or the colours that count. Choose this day or every archived day, and search.

You get a TICKER LIST, which is what you asked for - symbol, when it first hit, when it last hit, how many times, and the peak reading. Not a log of moments: 'Skittles 2h cyan or magenta' on Sep 4 is 455 moments but only 30 tickers, and the moment list is the same name every two minutes.

Real answer from your archive, RVOL 1h over 3 with buyers winning: 28 tickers on Sep 4, 35 on Sep 3, 27 on Sep 2, 71 on Sep 1. Top of Sep 4 was BILI (09:33 to 09:48, peak 6.0), ALAB (09:48 to 11:00, peak 5.5) and HUT (15:55 to 16:16, peak 5.3).

It runs on the server over the whole archive, because it has to. A day file is 8.8 to 25.5 MB and your browser only ever holds the newest 400 of about 11,770 entries - searching what was already on screen would have covered 3% of the day and shown you the result as if it were all of it.
The colours travel with the search. The server never learns what 'cyan' means; it is handed the exact lists the live board paints with, so a FIND result can never disagree with your board.
Speed: about a second the first time you run a query across every day, and instant after that. Searching one day is instant.
If a search returns more than 2000 rows it says so - 'showing the top 2000 of 2431' - rather than quietly handing you a shorter list.

releases.heading: The new 'nothing is wrong' chip could have gone quiet on a dead overnight feed - fixed before you hit it
releases.subheading: A review of my own change caught it. Same reload.
items: The fix I shipped an hour ago treated 8pm to 4am on a weeknight as 'market closed, nothing can be wrong'. That is wrong: the app really does pull overnight bars in that window - measured, 94 five-minute bars a night on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. So a feed that died at 8pm would have shown a calm grey chip until 4am, and the old amber rule WOULD have caught it. My change made that worse before you ever saw it.

It now knows the data week runs continuously from Sunday 8pm to Friday 8pm. Inside that, a tape that stops moving goes amber - overnight included. Only the Friday-night-to-Sunday-night gap is expected to sit still.

The overnight allowance is 45 minutes rather than 30, because the overnight feed is published about 16 minutes late by design and a build cycle sits on top of that. At 30 it would have gone amber every night for no reason.
Saturday still reads a quiet grey 'Last bar Fri 8:00 PM ET', which is the whole point of the original fix.

releases.heading: "DATA AS OF FRI 8:00 PM ET" was not a fault - and the board no longer pretends it is
releases.subheading: Your scanner was running the whole time. I checked it live before changing anything.
items: The scanner IS running. Checked while you were asking: the worker rebuilt and wrote its board cache at 13:29 ET, the board reported it had been built at 13:28 ET on Saturday, and it returned zero errors. Nothing was broken.

'Fri 8:00 PM ET' is the correct answer. 8:00 PM Friday is the end of the post-market session, and the overnight session does not restart until Sunday evening. So on a Saturday there is genuinely no newer bar in existence.

The bug was the wording and the colour. The old rule was 'newest bar more than 30 minutes old = paint an amber warning' - which is true every single evening and all weekend. A warning that fires on the normal case is not a warning, and it made you think the app had died.

It now says three different things. Market open and keeping up: 'Data 11:05 ET (3m)', quiet. Market closed: 'Last bar Fri 8:00 PM ET' in plain grey, with a tooltip saying nothing is wrong and the scanner is still running. Tape genuinely behind: 'Tape stale - last bar ...' in amber, which is the one worth chasing.

It can now catch a case it used to miss: a tape stuck since Monday is only about 26 hours old on Tuesday night, so any simple age rule calls it fine. The board now asks whether the market has had a CHANCE to make a newer bar, so that one shows up as stale.

releases.heading: Learn + Setup: a 'How to check app health' page
releases.subheading: Setup tab, bottom section - what to do when the app looks down, with the exact commands
items: Rule out the browser first, then Step 0 (the read-only health check command), Step 1 (the one command that restarts the whole app), and a by-symptom table for Error 1033, an expired TOS lamp, missing phone alerts and a stalled backup.
Written for the person at the AGX PC; nothing on it changes anything until you run the fix it names.

releases.heading: The filter panel scrolls again, and MACD was there all along - below the fold
releases.subheading: I had added two settings that this app already knew break scrolling on your phone
items: MACD IS in the filter. Open SKITTLES and look at 'Counts as a pass': green - MACD up 9 over 20, and dark green - MACD up, both ticked. You could not see them because they sat below the bottom of a panel that would not scroll down.

Why it would not scroll: in the earlier 'scroll fix' I added two CSS settings to the panel. This app's own notes record BOTH of them breaking scrolling on your phone before - one of them is described as having 'killed both directions'. I put them back in anyway. They are now removed, and a plain scroller is what is left.

The panel is also sized to the part of the screen you can actually see. On the iPhone, Safari's address bar and bottom toolbar make the real screen shorter than the page thinks it is, so a centred panel gets pushed down behind the bottom toolbar. That is the other half of both the 'cannot scroll up' and 'cannot scroll down' reports.

And it is a lot shorter: the colour labels were three lines each, so the panel was 1083px of content on your phone. Shortened to trader wording ('green - MACD up, 9 over 20'), and everything is now two columns, the panel is 927px and you scroll 390px instead of 615px to reach the bottom.
No settings were reset.

releases.heading: Skittles can now filter on MACD crosses, not just the EMA 9/20 cross
releases.subheading: You asked why MACD was missing - it was, and that is why the group kept returning nothing
items: The Skittles column paints FOUR different bullish events, and the filter was only testing one of them (cyan, the EMA 9/20 cross). MACD crosses were unreachable.

That is exactly why ticking SKITTLES gave you 0 tickers. Tonight your 8 matches have ZERO cyan cells - but four dark green, two green and one lime, all of which are MACD or EMA 4/8 crosses the filter could not see.

SKITTLES now has the same 'Counts as a pass' list that SQZ has, with each colour named by what fired: cyan (EMA 9 above 20), green (MACD up with 9 above 20), lime (EMA 4 above 8), dark green (MACD up). All four are ticked to start. The four bearish paints are listed too, unticked.
With that in, ticking SKITTLES now gives you 5 of 8 instead of 0: ALAB and TLN on a daily MACD cross, MPC and NTRA on a 2h MACD cross, NTRA also on a daily EMA 4/8, and HIMS on a 4h MACD cross.
Your settings were NOT reset this time. The new colour list slots in underneath what you already had.
The panel now also says these are the BLOCK colours, not the number's colour - the number being cyan just means the 9 EMA is already above the 20, which is not an event.

releases.heading: Ticking SKITTLES now actually filters - the tick box was being overridden
