releases.subheading: The 'push to top' / 'must have' radio is gone, replaced by a separate star switch
items: You ticked the SKITTLES box and the board still showed every ticker. That was a design mistake of mine: the 'push to top' setting underneath silently overrode the tick box, so a switched-ON group filtered nothing. A yellow warning explaining that was not good enough - the control itself was wrong.
The tick box now means the same thing in all three groups: this group is part of the rule. Tick SKITTLES and it filters, exactly like RVOL and SQZ.

'Push to top' is now its own separate checkbox - 'Star these and push them to the top' - and it works whether or not SKITTLES is filtering. So the original behaviour, 'show me the RVOL and SQZ names with the Skittles ones starred on top', is still what you get out of the box.
Nothing changes about the board by default. SKITTLES now starts unticked, which is the honest spelling of what it was already doing - the filter is RVOL or SQZ, and Skittles stars and lifts.
Your filter settings were reset once more, because the setting itself changed shape. Sorry - that is the second reset tonight and it should be the last.

Tonight, ticking SKITTLES correctly gives you 0 tickers: not one of the 8 has a cyan Skittles on any timeframe. The group's count in the panel header shows 0 before you tick it, so you can see that coming.

releases.heading: The FILTERS panel now tells you when it is not filtering anything
releases.subheading: You ticked Skittles D and still saw every ticker - here is why, and it was my bug
items: You switched RVOL and SQZ off, switched SKITTLES on and ticked D, and the board still showed all 8 tickers. Skittles was set to 'push to top', which only moves tickers up the board and never removes any. With RVOL and SQZ off, nothing at all was filtering - so every ticker passed. The panel meanwhile said 'ANY of: Skittles cyan on any of 1 timeframes', naming a rule it was not applying. That sentence was wrong and is fixed.
The panel now says, in a yellow box: 'Nothing is filtering - every ticker passes', and names the exact switch that fixes it.
Every group now shows how many tickers it would pass, right next to its name. Open it now and you will see SQZ 7, RVOL 0, Skittles 0 - which is the whole answer at a glance.

About Skittles D specifically: tonight NOT ONE of your 8 tickers has a cyan Skittles on any timeframe, D included. So if you choose 'must have', you will correctly get 0 tickers. That is the data, not a bug - a cyan Skittles block means the 9 EMA crossed above the 20 on that exact bar, which is rare.
The description also reads properly for a single timeframe now: 'Skittles cyan on D' instead of 'on any of 1 timeframes'.

releases.heading: A TOP button on the board, for when it will not scroll back up
releases.subheading: Plus an honest note: I could not reproduce the scrolling problem itself
items: When the MomX board is scrolled down on a phone, a small TOP pill appears above the tab bar. Tap it and the board jumps back to the toolbar. It works by moving the board directly rather than by scrolling, so it gets you back even when a swipe will not.

This is a way out, NOT a fix for the cause. You reported the board scrolled down and would not come back up. I tried five ways to reproduce it here and could not: swipe gestures on an emulated iPhone recover every time, panned sideways or not; the 15-second refresh does not drag the position back over a full minute; the page behind the board never scrolls; and Safari's own engine cannot be driven by a fake gesture, so it could not be tested that way.

One thing I did find, and it is mine: the new FILTERS button wraps your toolbar onto an extra line on a 390px phone, making the board 32px taller (a toolbar of 163px became 195px). Hiding the word FILTERS was tried and did not win the line back, so the label stays and the TOP button covers the inconvenience.

If it happens again, it would help to know: does it come back after you turn the phone sideways and back, or after closing and reopening the tab? That would tell me whether the board is genuinely stuck or the screen is not repainting.

releases.heading: The FILTERS panel scrolls properly on the phone again
releases.subheading: It could be scrolled down but not back up
items: The panel is now three fixed parts: a header, a scrolling middle, and a footer. Before, the whole panel was one scrolling box with a header stuck to the top of it - and on the iPhone that combination inside a pop-up wedges: you could get to the bottom and not back up to the RVOL rows.
The count and the Reset button no longer scroll away. They stay on screen while you tick boxes, which is when you actually want to see the count.

The panel is also sized against the visible screen now, not the full screen height. On the iPhone those are different when Safari's address bar is showing, and the difference was pushing the top of the panel up under the address bar where nothing could reach it.
Verified with real swipe gestures on two phone sizes: down to the bottom and all the way back to the top, with nothing hidden behind the header.

releases.heading: FILTERS: SQZ now defaults to ANY of the following, like your TOS scan
releases.subheading: And your saved filter settings are reset once so the change actually reaches your phone
items: SQZ was defaulting to ALL of 2h/4h. Your TOS scan lists SqzFired as an ANY row across 2h/4h/D/Wk, so it now matches: one timeframe is enough.

What that does, measured on Sep 4 at 1pm: the SQZ group alone goes from 125 of 208 tickers to 184, and the whole board from 129 to 187. Worth knowing because this group's pass list includes 'no squeeze at all', which is the normal state - so ANY here reads as '2h OR 4h is not squeezed', which almost everything satisfies. If the board feels too wide, the lever is unticking the SQZ group, not changing a number.

Your filter settings were reset to the new defaults once. They had to be: the panel remembers what you set, so a saved 'ALL' on your phone would have kept winning over the new default and nothing would have looked different.
You can still switch any group back to ALL from its own dropdown at any time.

releases.heading: FILTERS - your RVOL / SQZ / Skittles check, done for you on every refresh
releases.subheading: New button next to SCAN. Laid out like a thinkorswim scan, ANY of the following.
items: Press FILTERS and the board shows only the tickers that pass your three conditions. The number on the button tells you how many that is BEFORE you press it.

Click the sliders beside it to set the conditions: RVOL with a tick box and its own threshold per timeframe (1h/2h/4h at 2.5 to start), SQZ with the five squeeze states spelled out and 'fired' plus 'no squeeze' ticked, and Skittles across all eight timeframes. Every group has its own ANY of / ALL of, same as your scan.
The ticker count moves as you tick. That is the point - 2.5 or 3.0, three timeframes or four, you set it and watch what it does instead of guessing.

Skittles starts as 'push to top', not 'must have': tickers with a fresh cyan cross float to the top of the board and get a star, but nothing is thrown out for missing one. As a must-have it left 0 or 1 ticker on the board at 9:45am on each of the last three sessions - so the panel warns you if you switch it.

Why this exists: the scan behind the board has 35 ways to say yes and needs only one. At 1pm on Sep 4, 95 of its 208 tickers were there on a single condition, and MACD accounted for 189 firings against RVOL's 15. That is why the board is 200+ names and why your eye goes to RVOL, SQZ and Skittles instead.
Your settings are remembered. Whether the filter is pressed is not - a filter left on overnight would make the scan look broken in the morning.
Nothing new is fetched and the scan is not slowed: every ticker's numbers are already in the browser, so the filtering is instant.

releases.heading: "Why is it moving?" - the AI reads the headlines and tells you, or says it cannot
releases.subheading: Open any news headline on the scanner and press the button
items: Example, live: ChargePoint came back 'ChargePoint shares rallied significantly following a Q2 double beat on earnings and revenue expectations' - EARNINGS, high confidence, 8 headlines read, and it names the exact story it used.

When the headlines do NOT explain the move it says 'No news explains this move.' instead of inventing something. NBIS and AAPL both did exactly that tonight after reading 8 headlines each. That is the difference from the app you showed me, where a generic line about GPU compute capacity sat under a ticker up 5.83% and explained nothing.
On demand only - you press the button on a headline you opened. A 358-row board must never fire 358 AI calls.

This was built on Aug 27 and had never been connected to anything. It was also being starved: it read a cache holding only ~64 recently-viewed tickers, so it answered 'no news' for almost everything - including tickers whose headline was on your board at that moment. It now looks the headlines up properly.

releases.heading: The forming candle no longer drops to Vol 0 at every 5-minute boundary
releases.subheading: Chart volume keeps the fuller of its two readings instead of whichever arrived last
items: When a new 5-minute candle opens, the live tape knows almost nothing about its volume yet while the server's bar for the same candle is complete. The chart used to take the live reading, so the legend read Vol 0 for the first minute (measured 08:30:01 ET: 60,858 -> 0). It now keeps the larger of the two.
A minute with no volume reading no longer poisons its candle's total; it simply adds nothing.
Price still comes from the live tape, so the forming candle keeps ticking exactly as before.

releases.heading: A chart that wakes up now checks whether its candles are actually current
releases.subheading: And only reloads when they are not
items: Coming back to the app now decides what to do from the AGE OF THE CANDLES ON SCREEN rather than from how long the tab was away. A chart that is already current does nothing; a slightly behind one fetches quietly; a badly behind one asks for a full rebuild.
Three ways back are covered now, not one: switching to the tab, restoring it from the phone's memory (which fires no visibility event at all), and the signal coming back.
A request left over from a sleep is still discarded so it cannot block every later refresh - that was the twelve-hour CRWV freeze.
Before this, every glance at the app spent a chart request whether anything was stale or not.

releases.heading: The forming candle now shows its real volume instead of 0
releases.subheading: Derived from the day total Schwab was already sending and we were throwing away
items: The candle still being built showed 'Vol 0' - not because nothing traded, but because the code stamped a zero whenever a price tick opened a new minute. On QQQ that read Vol 0 over a bar the server had at 22,821.

Schwab's live feed already carries the running day total (verified: NVDA ticking 134,527,448 to 134,527,492 across four seconds) and nothing was reading it. The volume inside the current minute is now that total minus what it stood at when the minute opened.
When Schwab sends the finished minute's own volume, that always wins - the derived figure is only used while the candle is still forming.
If the day total is genuinely unavailable the bar is flagged as unknown rather than asserting a zero.

releases.heading: The news icon now tells you the source, the age, and whether the story is really about your ticker
releases.subheading: Hover it - and a round-up that only mentions your symbol is dimmed
items: Hovering the news icon used to show just the headline. It now leads with the source and the age - 'Yahoo Finance - 3h ago' - so a fresh story about your company no longer looks identical to a two-day-old round-up.
A story that merely names your ticker among many is now dimmed and says so in words: 'Market-wide story naming 10 tickers - it mentions this symbol, it is not about it.'
Dimmed rather than hidden, on purpose: a missing icon would read as 'nothing happened', which is a different wrong answer - the same reason a missing price shows a dash instead of 0.00%.
Still a badge in the Symbol cell, not a new column - the board stays width-locked as you asked on Aug 30.

releases.heading: News now covers the tickers Benzinga ignores - and stops pasting one story onto twenty rows
releases.subheading: A second, free news feed behind the existing one, plus a market-wide tag
items: You showed NBIS with news on MomoX3 and nothing on ours. You were right, and it was a coverage gap: our only feed was Benzinga, whose newest NBIS headline was two days old, so the 24-hour rule correctly hid it. Yahoo's free feed had a 6-hour-old Nebius story the whole time.

A second feed now fills in behind Benzinga for the tickers it does not cover. Measured on eight names: 8 of 8 now carry a headline, where before only 3 did. Benzinga still wins whenever it has the story, so nothing you already saw changes.

Market round-ups are now labelled instead of masquerading. A story naming more than three tickers ('10 Information Technology Stocks Whale Activity') is tagged market-wide rather than shown as if it were about your ticker. Before this, 120 of 358 rows were drawing from just 79 distinct headlines - the same defect visible on MomoX3, where AMD, MRVL and AMDL all show one identical Nvidia story.

Deliberately capped: the new feed asks for one ticker per request, so it fills 24 symbols per pass and covers the rest over the following hour. Doing all of them at once would be 74-144 requests a minute, which is exactly what got this machine blocked twice this week.

releases.heading: The 5-minute tape no longer shrinks to one candle on every refresh
releases.subheading: Plus the live badge learns to admit when the stream is dead
items: Measured 08:46 ET today: each 30-second refresh sent the browser a 1-candle tail of the 60-day 5-minute tape and the browser kept that 1 candle in place of the 13,806 it already held, so the 5m/10m/15m views quietly fell back to the 1-minute tape - and on a phone that had slept, to a tape with a gap in it. The tail is now merged onto the held tape like the 1-minute candles are.

The STREAMING badge used to switch on with the first packet and never switch off - a phone waking to a dead feed kept reading STREAMING all morning. A feed silent for two 30-second windows in a row now tells the chart it is down, so it falls back to REST refreshes honestly.

Groundwork for the tab-wake fix (decide from the age of the newest candle whether to fetch a tail or the whole tape, and reconnect the stream) is in and tested; it is wired into the chart after the open, not in the minutes before it.

releases.heading: Candles catch up in a minute or two, not ten
releases.subheading: The server stops recomputing labels every minute for tickers nobody has open
items: Measured 08:30 ET today: the server was at 94% of a CPU core and every ticker's candles were 2-10 minutes behind (SPY 7 min, HOOD 10 min), because it was redrawing the multi-timeframe CALL/PUT labels for about ten scanner tickers every minute whether or not anyone was looking at them.
A ticker that no one has open now keeps its last labels for up to ten minutes before they are recomputed. A chart you actually have open is untouched - its labels are recomputed exactly as before.
This needed one backend restart before the open; charts may show 'loading' for a few minutes right after it.

releases.heading: Charts open fast again instead of waiting 20-60 seconds
releases.subheading: Opening a chart no longer forces the server to rebuild its whole history first
items: When the live feed ran more than 90 seconds ahead of the saved candles - which is normal the moment you open a chart - the app asked the server to rebuild that ticker's entire history before showing you anything. Measured: 20.2 seconds, against 1.4 seconds for a plain reload of the same ticker.
It now reloads the candles the server already has, which fills almost all of the gap immediately. Only if a real hole survives two attempts does it ask for the full rebuild.
Nothing about your candles or your labels changed - this is purely about how quickly the chart gives up waiting.
Reload once to pick it up.

releases.heading: A chart left open overnight now refreshes itself when you come back to it
releases.subheading: It could sit frozen on last night's candles and last night's price, with the countdown still ticking
items: CRWV showed $84.35 and +2.47% at 8:24 AM while the market was at $85.73 and +1.38% - the whole panel was stopped at 7:55 PM the previous evening, twelve hours earlier, and nothing on screen said so.

Cause: when a phone sleeps mid-request the connection dies without the browser ever reporting a failure, so the chart's 'a request is already running' flag was never cleared and every later refresh returned immediately without doing anything.

Now: bringing the tab back to the front forces a fresh load, and a request left over from a sleep is discarded after 30 seconds so it can no longer block anything. The dashboard already worked this way; the chart did not.
Reload once to pick this up. After that, waking your phone is enough.

releases.heading: The chart strip stops showing Chg 0.00% and Vol 0 when it simply does not know
releases.subheading: Same false-zero as the ticker rail, in two more places on the chart header
items: QQQ read 'Chg 0.00%' at 8:12 AM while the price feed was reporting +0.42% for the same ticker at the same second. A missing percentage was being turned into a confident zero. It now shows nothing at all until a real move is reported.

'Vol 0' on the forming candle: the live bar is built from price ticks, which carry no volume, so it printed 0 over a bar the server had at 22,821. It now shows a dash while the bar is still forming. A genuine zero - nothing traded - still shows as 0, so the two stay tellable apart.
No restart needed; reload the page to pick it up.

releases.heading: Overnight candles TOS skipped are drawn again from the live tape
releases.subheading: Follow-up to the 02:35 candle fix, which had hidden them
items: The 02:35 fix stopped the live tape from touching any finished candle. Too strict: on the night of Sep 2 the TOS 5-minute tape holds only 32 of 96 candles while the 1-minute tape has all 96, so 64 candles that used to draw went missing. The live tape may now fill a candle TOS is missing - it still can never overwrite one that is there.
Checked on the real AMZN data: Sep 1 night 96 of 96, Sep 2 night 96 of 96, Sep 3 regular session 78 of 78 five-minute candles.

releases.heading: Schwab was sending every candle twice - now they are collapsed
releases.subheading: Found while tracing why the scanner started tripping Schwab's limits on Sept 1
items: Every price-history response from Schwab contains each candle two times over (measured: AAPL over four hours came back as 310 candles for 155 actual bars). Nothing removed the repeats, so they reached every chart and every tape.

Your RVOL was NOT affected - the scanner stores volume keyed by bar time, so a repeat overwrote rather than added. But two bars sharing one timestamp is exactly what makes a chart panel throw the 'cannot update oldest data' error.
Duplicates are now dropped where Schwab data enters the app. The repeats are identical, so no number changes - there is simply one bar where there were two.

releases.heading: When Schwab stops answering, the app now says so instead of showing 0.00%
releases.subheading: Plus an automatic back-off so we stop asking when Schwab tells us to slow down
items: Between 1:05 and 2:15 AM ET, Schwab blocked this address entirely - every price request refused. The charts kept drawing (those candles come from the backup feed) but every FAV TICKER read 0.00%, which looked like 'flat' when it actually meant 'no data'. A missing price now shows no percentage at all rather than a confident zero.

The TOS MARKET / TOS TRADING lamps stayed green through the whole outage, because they only ever checked whether your login was still valid - and it was, with 7 days left. They now also watch whether calls are actually getting through, so the lamp goes red when the data stops even though the login is fine.

If Schwab replies 'too many requests', the app now pauses briefly instead of carrying straight on - 5 seconds, then 15, then a full minute if it keeps happening, and back to normal the moment a request succeeds. Ignoring that warning is what turns into an hour-long block.

A chart whose data did not come from Schwab now says 'Backup feed - Schwab unavailable' instead of labelling it 'Schwab/TOS API', and carries the time of its newest candle so a frozen chart cannot look live.

Re-authenticating does NOT fix this kind of block (Schwab's login page is behind the same door), so the app no longer points you there for it. It clears on its own, or sooner if your connection gets a new address.
When Schwab starts answering again the app picks straight back up on its own - the pause lifts on the first successful request and the lamp goes green again, with no restart needed.

releases.heading: A stalled live feed can no longer flatten a finished candle
releases.subheading: Charts: TOS price history owns every closed candle; the live tick only moves the forming one
items: Overnight 2026-09-04 (01:05-02:15 ET) Schwab blocked this house's connection. While it was blocked, a single sparse live minute was painted over completed 5-minute candles and the legend read O=H=L=C, Vol 0. Closed candles now always come from TOS history on every timeframe (5m to monthly).

The live tick still drives the current candle, any candle newer than TOS has shipped, and any candle TOS is MISSING (the night of Sep 2 had 32 of 96 five-minute candles in the TOS tape; the one-minute tape fills the other 64). It just cannot overwrite a candle that is already there.
Not changed: the 20:00-04:00 ET overnight session still shows only the trades that actually printed (a few per hour on most names) - TOS's API does not serve that window.

releases.heading: One-command health check for when the app looks down
releases.subheading: scripts\check_health.ps1 - read-only, prints OK/DOWN per part and the exact command to run next
items: Run it from PowerShell (the command is Step 0 in docs/RUNBOOK.md). It checks the five ports, the three scheduled tasks, the tunnel, Google Drive backups and both Schwab logins, and shows the last error lines.
Runbook updated for the renamed TOS MARKET / TOS TRADING lamps, the 2-day blink and the 1-day phone push.

releases.heading: Nightly backup now covers every user's saved keys and Schwab logins
releases.subheading: Plus a step-by-step 'move to a new laptop' page in docs
items: The secrets zip in Google Drive now also holds the per-user key vault and each user's Schwab login files, so a rebuild from Drive alone no longer loses them.
docs/MOVE_TO_NEW_LAPTOP.md: what git carries, what to copy by hand, and the exact commands to bring AGX up on another machine.

releases.heading: Days left on each Schwab login, right beside its lamp
releases.subheading: TOS MARKET 6d · TOS TRADING 3d - the 7-day expiry is now visible every day
items: Each Schwab lamp shows how long its login has left (days; hours once under a day). Hover for the exact date and time in ET.
Under two days it turns amber and BLINKS; past expiry it reads EXPIRED and keeps blinking. Re-authenticate in Settings before it gets there - an expired login takes the charts down.

releases.heading: Phone alert the day before a Schwab login expires
releases.subheading: ntfy push to admin phones at 24h left, and once more if it actually expires
items: One day before TOS MARKET or TOS TRADING login runs out you get a phone push naming which one, when it expires (ET), and that Settings is where to renew it.
If it does expire, one more push says the data is down until you re-authenticate. Each login sends each message once; renewing re-arms it for the next week.
Checked every 10 minutes by the app server; a restart never repeats a push.

releases.heading: Header lamps renamed: TOS MARKET and TOS TRADING
releases.subheading: Same two lamps, named after the two Schwab apps they watch
items: TOS DATA is now TOS MARKET - your Market Data app (charts, quotes, option chains).
TOS STREAM is now TOS TRADING - your Accounts & Trading app (the live tick stream).
The DATA ONLY lamp is gone - it was decoration, wired to nothing.

releases.heading: Schwab: an expired login no longer keeps knocking on Schwab's door
releases.subheading: The scanner was sending Schwab about two rejected requests a second, all night, with a dead token
items: Once the Market Data login expires, every Schwab request the app makes is refused BEFORE it leaves this machine - nothing goes to Schwab until you re-authenticate.
Before this, each of the scanner's 700-odd volume checks per build still went out, was rejected, and repeated on the next build - measured at 39 connections in 20 seconds.
After you re-authenticate, the running scanner picks up the new login by itself; no restart needed.

releases.heading: Schwab: starting one login no longer cancels the other
releases.subheading: The app kept only ONE login in progress for both Market Data and Accounts & Trading
items: Press Authenticate on one profile while part way through the other and the first was silently thrown away - the paste-back then failed with a meaningless "Expecting value: line 1 column 1" error.
Each profile now keeps its own login in progress, and so does each user.
Removed an unused address that quietly restarted a login in progress just by being visited.

releases.heading: Schwab re-authenticate deadlines were showing 5 hours early
releases.subheading: Settings said your Market Data login was good until 2:51 PM when it actually died at 7:51 PM
items: The expiry times were sent without a timezone, so your browser read the server clock as UTC and subtracted five hours. Both the Market Data and Accounts & Trading dates were wrong the same way.
The warning banners themselves were always on time - they count down on the server. Only the printed date was wrong.

releases.heading: Skittles cells pulse too when the cross has just fired
releases.subheading: Same signal as the RVOL blink, on all eight timeframes
items: A Skittles cell now pulses when its colour comes from a cross AND the bar that cross fired in opened within the last 15 minutes. Same look, same 15-minute window, same rule as the RVOL blink.

Measured on your own board before building it, so it is not a guess: 3 cells pulse when the 2-hour bar rolls (11:00 and 15:00), and 7 when the 2-hour and 4-hour roll together at 13:00. That is in line with the RVOL blink, which measured about 5.

One thing to expect rather than be surprised by: the daily, 2D, 3D, 4D, weekly and monthly bars all roll at midnight together, so for the fifteen minutes after 00:00 ET a lot of cells pulse at once - about 73 on a 50-row board. That is accurate rather than broken; those bars really did all just open. It was left alone rather than special-cased because it happens at midnight.
During the hours you actually trade, only the 2-hour and 4-hour Skittles can ever be fresh, which is exactly when a cross firing means something.

releases.heading: Skittles cells now show how old the cross is, on all eight timeframes
releases.subheading: A cyan 4h that fired 20 minutes ago reads very differently from one that fired 3h50 ago
items: Every Skittles cell whose colour comes from a cross now carries the same small age underneath it that the RVOL cells got - 2h, 4h, D, 2D, 3D, 4D, W and M.

It means something slightly different from the RVOL one, and that difference is deliberate. An RVOL number is volume piling up, so its age says when that volume arrived. Skittles has no volume - its colour comes from a cross that fired somewhere inside the current bar - so its age is the bar's own: "this bar opened 20m ago, so the cross is at most 20 minutes old".

It cannot narrow it further than that. A 4-hour EMA cross is defined on 4-hour closes; there is no finer version of it to look up, and inventing one would be a different indicator rather than a better answer.
Only cells where a cross actually fired get an age. Your script leaves the rest black, and dating those would have added about 2,400 numbers that say nothing.

Ages now count in days as well - "1d20", "3d20" - because the weekly and monthly columns are days old by definition. They previously stopped at 24 hours and would have shown nothing at all on exactly the columns you asked for.

releases.heading: The small number under RVOL now says HOW LONG AGO, not what time
releases.subheading: "12m" means it is happening now. "4h31" means it is old news.
items: It used to show a clock time - "4:00" - and that was confusing twice over. It could mean 4 in the morning or 4 in the afternoon, and it made you do the arithmetic against the header clock on every single row just to answer "is this new?".
It now shows the age directly. FDX's 2h reads 3.1 with "4h31" under it: that volume arrived four and a half hours ago. A fresh one reads "12m".

Nothing to work out and nothing to confuse with a time of day. It also lines up with the two signals already there: the number brightens under 15 minutes, and the cell pulses when it is both fresh and coloured. So blinking plus "12m" means it is happening right now.
The exact clock time is still there if you want it - hover the cell and the tooltip gives you both, in 24-hour so it cannot be misread.
And there is now a line under the table explaining what the small number is. That matters on the phone, where there is no hovering and it was previously just an unexplained number.

releases.heading: A 7.0 RVOL means "off the scale" - hover it to see how far off
releases.subheading: CHPT's D read 7.0 while it was actually trading 31 times its average volume
items: Comparing FDX's D of 1.7 against CHPT's D of 7.0 turned up something you could not see from the board: a relative-volume score over 50 bars can never exceed 7.0. That is arithmetic, not a setting - once one bar dominates the window, the score pins at 7 no matter how extreme it gets.

So FDX's 1.7 is a real measurement (1.6 times its average volume), but CHPT's 7.0 is the number hitting a wall. CHPT actually traded 30.8 times its average. At 100 times it would still have shown 7.0.

Hovering a cell that has hit the ceiling now tells you the real multiple - "31x the 50-bar average volume" - so you can tell an 8x day from a 30x one. The number shown on the board is unchanged, still exactly what your ThinkorSwim script plots.
Only cells that are actually capped get the hover text. Everywhere else the number already says everything.

This also explains something odd from earlier: when I measured what turning on the 5-minute alert would cost, 133 readings sat at exactly 7.0 - seven names pinned together at 4:22am. A thin overnight tape reaches the ceiling trivially. Same effect, and part of why that alert would have been unusable.

releases.heading: The D column was the one missing its time - now it has the most useful one
releases.subheading: It tells you when half of today's volume actually traded
items: You spotted that some RVOL cells had no time under them. Checked every visible cell on the board: none were missing except the D column, which was hidden on purpose - but for a reason that had gone stale.

When the time first went in it meant "when this bar opened", and a daily bar always opens at midnight, so D would have said 12:00 on every row forever. It was hidden. Then the meaning changed to "when the volume arrived", and nobody went back and un-hid it.

For a daily bar that now answers something genuinely useful: when did half of today's volume actually trade. CHPT's +74% day reads 11:20 - the bulk of 43.8 million shares went through in the late morning. HPE reads 2:15 of 72.1 million. FDX reads 3:35 of 2.1 million, which fits its closing-auction spike.

The daily span is kept separate from the one used for the alert's pace calculation, which deliberately has no daily entry - projecting a part-finished day to a full one says nothing, whereas asking when half of it traded does.

releases.heading: An RVOL cell now BLINKS when the spike is happening right now
releases.subheading: Coloured background plus volume that arrived in the last 15 minutes
items: A cell pulses when two things are true at once: your script has painted it a colour, and the volume behind it arrived within the last 15 minutes. That is a spike happening now rather than a bucket that filled up hours ago.

The threshold is not a new number I picked - it is yours. Your column script only gives a cell a background at relVol 2.0 and above (cyan and green when the bar is bullish, magenta and red when it is not; black below that). So "has a background" already IS the threshold, and the app now reads the colour your script assigned instead of re-deriving it. All four colours count, not just cyan.

Why it is gated at all: I replayed 520 moments from today's session. Blinking on freshness alone would have flashed about 23 cells at once on a 30-row board, because almost every RVOL cell is technically "fresh" during the session. With the colour gate it is about 5 - rare enough to mean something.
It is a soft pulse around the number, not a hard flash, so the value stays readable while it draws your eye. It stops by itself once the volume ages past 15 minutes - nothing to dismiss.
The History tab never blinks. Those rows are a record of a past moment, and animating them would suggest something is happening now.
If you have asked your phone or computer for reduced motion, you get a steady ring instead of a pulse rather than losing the signal entirely.

releases.heading: The RVOL time now says when the volume CAME - and lights up when it just did
releases.subheading: "3:00" was only telling you when the bar opened, which is a bound, not an answer
items: The little time under each RVOL number was showing when that bar opened. That is technically true and practically useless: FDX's 2-hour bar opened at 3:00pm, but 67% of its entire volume landed in ONE five-minute window at 4:00pm. "3:00" only told you nothing was older than 3:00.
It now shows when the volume actually arrived - the point at which half the bar's volume was in. FDX's 2h, 4h and 1h all now read 4:00, because the closing auction dominates all three of them.

And to answer "how do I know this is the latest": the time is BRIGHT when the volume arrived within the last 15 minutes, and dim when it did not. No subtracting against the clock while you scan fifty rows.
15 minutes is not a new number - it is what this app already means by new: the same window as the NEW badge on a fresh match and your alert cooldown.
Brightness rather than a new colour, deliberately: colour on this board belongs to your thinkScript ladders, and a fourth hue would compete with them.

releases.heading: Fixed: the new bar-time was invisible on exactly the cells that matter
releases.subheading: It showed on plain cells and vanished on every cyan, green and red one
items: The little clock time added minutes earlier was inheriting the cell's text colour - which on a coloured cell is BLACK, because that is correct for a number sitting on a bright cyan or green pill. The time sits outside the pill on the dark row, so it was black on near-black and effectively gone.
Which meant it was missing from precisely the cells you would look at: FDX's cyan 2h 3.1, TMO's red 2.2, DHI's cyan 3.7. It only showed where it was least needed.
It now uses its own colour - the same grey as the "4:23" beside a ticker that it was meant to match.

releases.heading: Every RVOL number now tells you WHEN its bar opened
releases.subheading: So a cyan 3.1 that arrived two hours ago stops looking like one happening now
items: Each RVOL cell now carries a tiny clock time underneath it - the same quiet style as the "4:23" beside a ticker. It is when that bar opened.

This is the FDX problem you spotted. Its 2h read a cyan 3.1 at 6:44pm, and you had no way to tell that the 3.1 arrived at 4:55pm during the closing auction and had not moved since. It now reads 3.1 with "3:00" under it - the 3 o'clock bar, not a spike happening now.

Same for HPE at 12:35: a cyan 4h 3.1 that was actually the MORNING's volume, sitting three and a half hours into its bar, while every fast column was negative. The real fresh spike came at 3:10pm when the 5m hit 4.3 with price at -0.53%, and HPE ran to +5.5% from there.
The rule this makes visible: a high number on a long timeframe means "this bar holds a lot of volume", not "volume is arriving". Early in a bar those are the same thing. Late in a bar they are not.

Only added to cells that are already visible - the deliberately blacked-out weak readings stay blank, so the board does not turn into a wall of numbers. Not shown on the D column, where a bar always opens at midnight and the label would say nothing.
The time comes from the bar itself, never from your computer's clock, so it cannot drift when the data feed runs behind.

releases.heading: Fixed properly: the 4-hour volume condition was comparing against the wrong bar
releases.subheading: Solved with your two TOS readings - and it replaces this afternoon's temporary workaround
items: You ran your TOS scan twice and sent the results - 10 matches at 18:15, 9 at 18:21 with CHTR dropping out. That was enough to prove our version wrong: it rejected WELL and REGN both times while your TOS matched them.

The cause: we build a 4-hour bar for any window that had any trading, so a quiet overnight window becomes a full bar and our series carries one more bar per day than yours. "2 bars ago" was therefore landing on a different time of day depending on whether the stock traded overnight - a near-empty 102-share bar for some, a full trading session for others. Comparing against one bar further back lines us up with you.
Checked against both your readings: it reproduces all 19 of your matches and correctly rejects the CHTR you dropped. No exceptions, no misses.
It also fixes the over-matching. On a 129-name sample this returns FEWER rows than what was running before (12 against 14) while catching more of your actual matches (8 of 9 against 6 of 9).

And this afternoon's temporary workaround is now deleted rather than left sitting on top. Your scan returning 9-10 matches in the evening proved the scanner was never really blind at night - it was this alignment all along. The 1-hour price condition was tested the same way and correctly stays as it was.

releases.heading: The H/L column explained correctly - and confirmed as your own script
releases.subheading: The Learn page had it backwards: an empty bar means the MIDDLE of the range, not the low
items: You sent the High/Low Graph column's script and its settings, and our version matches it line for line - highest high and lowest low over the last 8 bars, midpoint between them, then (close - midpoint) / (high - midpoint), on the 2-hour aggregation with extended hours on. Nothing needed changing in the calculation.

The Learn page was wrong about it in two ways, and one of them would have made you read the column backwards. It said the bar shows "today's range" - it is actually the last 8 two-hour bars with extended hours, roughly 16 hours, not the day. And it said an empty bar means price is at the LOW - an empty bar means the MIDDLE. The low is a full bar in the other direction, coloured red.
The green/red colouring is ours, not yours - your script just plots the number and ThinkorSwim draws it as a graph. That is now written down so nobody 'corrects' it to something you never asked for.

The code had been contradicting itself, labelling this column a guess in one place and "ported literally" in another. An automated audit read the contradiction and reported the column as invented. Your script settles it: it was never a guess.

Also strengthened its test. The check for price sitting at the bottom of the range asserted the value was "less than 50", which every possible reading passes, so it could never have caught a mistake there - exactly the half of the scale that decides which names sink to the bottom of your default sort.

releases.heading: Fixed: the scanner went completely blind for about eight hours every night
releases.subheading: 17:00 to 05:00 ET, no matches at all - by construction, not because nothing was happening
items: One of the scan's conditions compares the current 4-hour bar's volume against the bar two back. In the evening, "two back" is the morning session - so an after-hours window was being asked to out-trade a full trading day. It can't, so it failed, and because every condition has to pass, the whole board returned nothing from about 17:00 until 05:00 ET.

It was never filtering there, it was switching the scanner off. Measured over 30 days: in the 17:00 bar that condition passed 0 times out of 126, and in the 21:00 bar 1 out of 95. Meanwhile ThinkorSwim returned 16 matches at 17:29 ET on one of those same days - so the condition was wrong, not just strict.
Confirmed from your own history: of 27,375 recorded matches over four days, only 2.3% fall between 17:00 and 05:00, and the 18:00, 20:00 and 23:00 hours contain literally none.

That condition is now skipped in those two evening bars only. Its formula is completely unchanged, and it still applies during the day and overnight into the morning, where it was measured to genuinely discriminate (34% to 100% pass rates). Removing a filter that rejected 0 of 126 cannot let anything meaningful through.
Evening and overnight setups should now appear on the board instead of being invisible. Everything else still has to pass - a name still needs a real momentum, squeeze or volume reason to match.

Honest limit: this stops the blackout, it does not explain it. The underlying condition still does not match what your TOS does, and settling that needs the actual script from the Price_Change row in your Stock Hacker scan.

releases.heading: Scan fix: the 5m and 15m volume conditions were firing too easily
releases.subheading: Your TOS requires 5 standard deviations on those two rows; we were using 3
items: Your scan's RVOL rows are not all set the same. Reading them straight off your Stock Hacker: the 5m and 15m rows are configured with numDev = 5, while 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h and D use numDev = 3. We were applying 3 to all seven.

That made the two fastest and noisiest timeframes fire matches your TOS would never return - a short volume burst clears 3 standard deviations easily on a 5-minute bar. The error only ever ADDED rows to your board, never hid any.
It was invisible until you sent the actual scan rows, because the script text itself says numDev = 3 - that is the study's default, and the 5 is an override set per row inside the scan.
Nothing else about the volume condition changed: the 50-bar length is the same on every row, and the "more buying than selling" test is untouched.

Also checked against the scripts you sent and confirmed already correct: the Skittles column (8-period weighted stochastic across 2h/4h/D/2D/3D/4D/W/M), the Squeeze firing scan, the RVOL column formula and its colours, and the Quote trend column.

releases.heading: The Watchlist now refreshes about 40% faster
releases.subheading: It was rebuilding indicator columns for ~290 names you were not looking at, every cycle
items: The 358-name Watchlist took 297 seconds to build and then deliberately waited another 120, so the RVOL and Squeeze numbers you trade off were up to 7 minutes old.

Measured where the time went: building the display columns (RVOL, SQZ, Skittles, H/L, Quote) is 53% of the cost per ticker - and it was being paid for every one of the ~290 tickers that were not matching the scan and that you only see when you untick "Scan matches only".

Those columns are now carried over from the previous build for non-matching names, which takes the build to roughly 171 seconds. Anything MATCHING is rebuilt every cycle, and so is any name that has just started matching - a new match can never show you stale indicators.

Price and % Chg are still recalculated for every ticker every cycle, so the two numbers that move fastest are never carried over. And every 4th build rebuilds everything from scratch, so a non-matching row's indicators can be at most three cycles behind.
If a ticker's carried-over columns are not available for any reason, it is simply rebuilt normally - the shortcut only ever applies where there is a proven answer to reuse.

releases.heading: Premarket: the board is now ORDERED by today's move too, not just labelled with it
releases.subheading: Completing this afternoon's fix, which only reached half the path
items: This afternoon's fix made every row PRINT today's premarket change instead of yesterday's. It turns out the same number is calculated twice - once for what the row shows, once for deciding the order - and only the first was fixed. So before the open the board was still being SORTED by yesterday's move while each row displayed today's.

That is more than cosmetic. The ordering decides which names make the main list rather than the overflow, and only the main list gets live streaming quotes. Premarket, the wrong names were getting the live treatment.

Fixed at the root: the number is no longer worked out twice. The ordering now reads the row's own value, so the two cannot drift apart again. A regression test pins it - two stocks where yesterday's ranking and today's ranking disagree, and the test fails if the old order comes back.

Found by an automated audit of every scanner column against the ThinkorSwim scripts they implement. It also confirmed some good news: our RVOL formula, the 2-hour bar clock and the % Chg column all match your TOS - % Chg matched on 16 of 16 tickers this afternoon.

releases.heading: Fixed: before the open, % Chg was showing YESTERDAY's move
releases.subheading: Every premarket morning, on every ticker
items: Until the opening bell, the % Chg column was not showing today's change at all - it was showing the previous session's closing change, frozen, and then silently correcting itself at 09:30. CRDO sat at exactly -20.04% from 07:21 to 08:09 while its price never moved off $165. CLS showed -5.07% all premarket at $280.78, then jumped to +2.89% at 09:37 on a price of $282.24 - an eight-point jump on a stock that had moved 50 cents.

Confirmed rather than guessed: -20.04%, -5.07%, -4.32%, -3.55% and -5.42% were the exact closing changes of CRDO, CLS, NOW, ZETA and CRWD on the PREVIOUS day, matching to two decimal places on all five.

The cause: the column read the daily bars and compared the newest to the one before. Before the open there is no bar for today yet, so the newest one IS yesterday - and the answer was yesterday's change. Because it looked stable and fixed itself at the open, it never looked like a bug.
Now, when today's daily bar has not formed yet, the live premarket price is compared against yesterday's CLOSE, which is the right number. CLS at 07:21 would have read +1.08%, not -5.07%.

Regular hours is byte-for-byte unchanged and cannot move - the new path only runs when today's daily bar is missing. If the live price is unavailable premarket the column now shows nothing rather than a number that looks like today's and is not.
This also matters for the History archive: every premarket row recorded before today carries the wrong % Chg, so treat premarket entries in older history with suspicion.

releases.heading: Removed the “Live RVOL” tick that shipped earlier this afternoon
releases.subheading: It did not match ThinkorSwim, and matching ThinkorSwim is the point
items: A “Live RVOL” checkbox was added at 14:52 to show what volume was on track to close at, rather than what the still-forming bar reads so far. It has been removed. Ticking it produced numbers that disagreed with your TOS - HPE read 4.2 on the 2h with Live on, 0.9 with it off, and 1.2 on your actual TOS screen.

Checked properly against your TOS screenshot across 22 tickers: the plain column was closer on 17 of them. The projection overshoots because it divides the part-finished bar by how much of it has elapsed - a 2-hour bar only 18 minutes in gets multiplied by nearly seven before it is scored.

The RVOL columns are back to being exactly what they were: ThinkorSwim parity, one number, no toggle. Nothing else was touched - the scan, the alerts and every other column are unchanged, and the phone alerts always used a separate path that was never affected either way.

releases.heading: Fixed: the ticker card could show yesterday's option walls as today's
releases.subheading: Caught on CRWV
items: The first request for a ticker's option chain can come back as a complete, healthy-looking chain from the PREVIOUS day - CRWV returned a spot of 80.57 while it was trading at 83.78, with the expiry mislabelled as 2 days out. The server marks those payloads stale; the card was not reading that flag, so it would have drawn day-old walls and a day-old expected move as current, then held them for ten minutes.

The card now waits for a current chain, never stores a stale one, and if a chain is genuinely only available stale it will be shown with its timestamp rather than passed off as live. Levels you trade off should not be a day old without saying so.

releases.heading: New “Movers” list: the market's biggest gainers, scanned automatically
releases.subheading: So a CHPT can be found without you having typed the ticker
items: There is a new list in the picker called Movers. It fills itself with the day's biggest gainers every 5 minutes during market hours and runs your normal scan over them - so a name you have never added can still show up with its signals, its card, its history and its alerts. Right now it is holding CHPT +68.5% and ZOOZ +24.5% as matches.
This is why CHPT was late today: it was not in your watchlist until 12:56, and a watchlist scanner cannot find what it is not watching. Nothing was broken - your list just did not contain it.

Heavily filtered, because raw “top gainers” is mostly untradeable: the $3 floor your scan already uses, no warrants or preferreds, and no 2x/3x leveraged wrappers. Those wrappers matter - 20 of the first 26 names were things like “2X Long MSTR ETF” dressed up as ordinary tickers. Today 50 raw gainers became 5 real ones.
It never changes the tab you are on, and if the data feed fails the list is left alone rather than emptied.

releases.heading: Setup: the Schwab callback URL had a stray slash
releases.subheading: It now matches what the app actually sends
items: Step 5 of Setup told you to register https://127.0.0.1/ with a slash on the end, but the app sends https://127.0.0.1 without one. Schwab compares those two strings exactly, so anyone following the old wording would have registered a callback that could never match, and the login would fail with nothing useful said about why.
Changed in the in-app Setup steps only. The address you land on after approving still shows the slash - that part was always right and is unchanged.

releases.heading: The chart's scrollbar is thinner too
releases.subheading: 14px instead of 22 on desktop; the phone is unchanged
items: The scrubber under the chart is now 14 pixels instead of 22. It keeps the cyan thumb, the lighter track and the edge - those are what made it findable after you could not spot it five times, so only the thickness came off, not the visibility.
The phone keeps the thicker bar. You tap that one to pan the chart, and a thin bar is hard to hit; making it thinner there would trade a look for a control.

releases.heading: Scanner windows you are not looking at refresh once a minute
releases.subheading: The one in front stays at 15 seconds
items: With several scanner windows open, only the one in front refreshes every 15 seconds; the ones behind it drop to once a minute. Click a window and it goes straight back to 15 seconds. Measured: over 100 seconds a background window fetched once where the front one fetched seven times, and raising it swapped the two immediately.
The page's own board is unchanged, and ticker cards were never affected - they read from the board that is already there.

releases.heading: Slimmer scrollbars everywhere
releases.subheading: 8px instead of Windows' 17, matching the chart panes
items: Scrollbars across the app are now thin, with the little arrow buttons removed - 8 pixels, the same as the chart panes already used, instead of the ~17 Windows gives a container nobody styled. Places that deliberately have no scrollbar at all still have none.

releases.heading: H/L on the ticker card is a bar again, not a number
releases.subheading: Same graph the board draws
items: The card was printing H/L as “1.0”. It is a graph everywhere else - the value runs from -1 at the low to +1 at the high, and the bar fills from the centre so you can see how far up the range it sits, which a printed number cannot show. The card now draws the same bar, in the same colour, with the exact value still on hover.

releases.heading: Fixed within the hour: my last change quietly dropped a field from every scanner row
releases.subheading: Caught by the test suite before it could cause a visible problem
items: Adding the 1-hr high/low to the scanner's data contract accidentally deleted the “badge” field next to it, so every row shipped without it. Nothing you would have seen - the lightning bolt no longer reads that field - but anything else relying on it would have broken. Restored, and the contract test that catches this now also covers the new field.

releases.heading: The Watchlist scan does a third less work per cycle
releases.subheading: It was computing RVOL and the squeeze twice for every ticker - once for the scan, once for the columns
items: Measured 486 -> 327 milliseconds of processor time per ticker, so the board refreshes sooner after each build.
Every value on all 357 tickers was compared before and after, field by field: zero differences. The scan still matches thinkorswim exactly.

releases.heading: Fixed: the card's High-OI walls were reading the wrong strikes
releases.subheading: And the 1-hr high/low finally shows a number
items: You spotted it on KVUE: the card showed 22.5C with an open interest of ONE, while 20C sitting on 10,955 never appeared. It was ranking a small pre-filtered slice of the chain (18 rows) instead of the chain itself (308). It now reads the same rows the High-OI board on the charts reads, and reproduces your list exactly: 20C 10,955 · 19.5C 503 · 19C 5,347, and 18.5P · 18P 5,862.

The 1-hr high and low now show real numbers instead of “--”. The value was being calculated correctly all along but was missing from the list of fields the scanner is allowed to send, so it never left the server. A test now fails the moment a calculated field is not on that list.

releases.heading: The ⚡ works in History too - click any row for that moment's card
releases.subheading: Stamped with the snapshot time, so it can't be mistaken for now
items: Every History row is a full archived snapshot, so clicking its lightning bolt opens the same card built from what the board looked like at that minute - the cells, the news as it stood then, and the signals that had fired. The title says “snapshot” and the header carries the time it was taken.

Two things are deliberately left off a snapshot rather than filled in with today's numbers: the 1-hr high and low, which were never recorded at the time, and - on rows from a previous day - the option walls, because open interest changes overnight so today's walls were not the ones in force then. Same-day rows keep their walls.

releases.heading: The Watchlists menu uses the app's own font and colours again
releases.subheading: It was drawn outside the scanner, where none of the scanner's styling reached it
items: The list names were in the terminal's monospace font instead of the app font, BUILT-IN was full white so it shouted as loudly as the list name, and every row was boxed in white.
The Momo settings sheet and the news popover were drawn the same way and are corrected too.

releases.heading: Fixed: “no option-chain walls for this one” on tickers that have plenty
releases.subheading: And the card no longer stretches into a big empty gap
items: A ticker the board has not opened before takes about 20 seconds for its option chain to build. The card gave up after four and a half, said there were no walls, and then remembered that answer for ten minutes - so BOIL and IBM showed “no option-chain walls for this one” when both have plenty. It now waits the full time, tells you it is reading the chain, and only remembers an answer that actually found something.
The card layout no longer springs a large empty gap with the fired-signals line floating in the middle of it. That happened whenever the walls were missing.
The walls themselves are unchanged: biggest open interest within ±EM2, calls above the last price and puts below.

releases.heading: The ticker card now has the High-OI walls, like your card
releases.subheading: Calls above the last price, puts below, within ±EM2
items: Open a ticker card and you get its option walls: the biggest open-interest strikes within ±EM2 of the last price, calls above and puts below, each with a bar showing how big it is against the largest one. NVDA right now reads 230C 57k as the wall, with 220P 21k underneath, and the last price line between them with the ±EM2 range.
It uses exactly the same selection as the High-OI board on the charts - same function, same ±EM2 band - so the two can never disagree about which strikes matter.
Open interest only changes overnight, so the chain is read once when you open a card and shared by every card for ten minutes rather than polled. Nothing is requested until a card is actually open.

releases.heading: Click the ⚡ on a row and get that ticker's card in its own window
releases.subheading: And the ⚡ now means what it means on your card - the signals that fired
items: The lightning bolt used to mean “this symbol has weekly options”. It now means what it means on the card you work from: the signals that fired - MACD 4h · 9x20 4h · 4x8 4h · MACD 2D · SQZ D. Same data the scan already had, finally shown in your words.

Click it and that ticker opens as a card in a small window: symbol, change, price and sector across the top, every RVOL / SQZ / SKIT cell in exactly the colours the board uses, the news headline with its age, the fired signals, the last hour's high and low, and how long it has been on the board. The window drags, resizes and stacks like the scanner windows, and clicking the same bolt again brings its card forward rather than opening a second one.

Still to come on the card: the High-OI walls block from your screenshot. It comes from the options chain rather than the scanner, so it is a separate piece of work - left off rather than shown as an empty box.
The 1-hr high and low read “--” until the scanner is restarted, because the running scanner predates them.

releases.heading: Watchlists is a dropdown now, not a popup
releases.subheading: It hangs under the list button and stops dimming your board
items: Everything it had is still there - switch list, Rename, Delete, and New list name / Add list.
Closes when you pick a list, tap anywhere else, or press Escape; it follows the button if the board scrolls under it.

releases.heading: Scanner windows can now leave AGX - a DETACH button on each one
releases.subheading: For the second monitor, or beside thinkorswim
items: Every pop-out window now has a DETACH button in its title bar. Press it and that window leaves AGX and becomes its own window you can drag anywhere - another monitor, on top of thinkorswim, wherever. It keeps its own list, and next time you detach that list it opens back where you left it.

Why it could not do this before, and why installing AGX to the desktop did not help: the pop-out windows are drawn inside the page, and a web page cannot draw outside its own window. Only a window the browser itself creates can leave, which is what Detach makes.

The cost, measured rather than guessed: a detached window has a 72-pixel title strip, of which about 32 is Windows' own title bar. No tabs, no address bar, no bookmarks - a normal browser window costs 95. The in-app windows are unchanged and still have no bars at all, so you choose per window: quick look inside the app, all-day monitoring detached.

releases.heading: Several scanner windows at once, like thinkorswim - and the board behind stays put
releases.subheading: Pop out Mag7, switch to Watchlist, pop that out too
items: The pop-out button now opens a window for the list you are on. Switch to another list and press it again and you get a SECOND window, each locked to its own list, overlapping the way detached watchlists do in thinkorswim. Click a window to bring it to the front; each remembers its own size and position; Esc closes the front one.

Fixed: the scanner area behind the pop-up went black. The old version MOVED the one board into the window instead of leaving one on the page. Every window now has its own board, which is also the only way two lists can be on screen at the same time.

Pressing pop-out again on a list that already has a window brings that window forward instead of opening a duplicate. Windows are drawn by AGX, so there are no browser bars on them - the trade-off is that they stay inside the AGX window and cannot be dragged onto a second monitor.
Worth knowing: each open window is a live board on its own refresh, so several at once is several times the work. Say the word if it feels heavy and background windows can refresh more slowly.

releases.heading: The scanner pop-out is a real pop-up window now, not a full-screen takeover
releases.subheading: Correcting this morning's version, which was just Maximize under a different button
items: It opens as a window floating over the app: drag the title bar to move it, drag the bottom-right corner to size it, and the app stays visible and usable behind it. Where you put it and how big you make it are remembered for next time. Double-click the title bar to re-centre it, and close with the × or Esc.

The earlier version filled the whole screen, which made it identical to the Maximize button sitting next to it - and the icon had changed to a maximize icon too, so it looked like the pop-out had simply been removed. The familiar pop-out icon is back.

It can never be dragged off the edge and lost - it stops at the screen edge. On the phone it still opens edge-to-edge, since a draggable window on a 375px screen would not help; the title bar and close button are there either way.

releases.heading: Nothing in the app opens a Chrome tab any more
releases.subheading: The option chain and MAG7 pop-outs join the scanner
items: The option chain pop-out now fills the screen inside the app instead of opening a browser window. The header stays pinned at the top while you scroll the strikes. Press the same button again, or Esc, to come back.
The MAG7 pop-out now opens the Big screen workspace - the in-app full-screen view that was already sitting next to it - rather than a separate window.

The single-chart pop-out button was already switched off in the code and never appeared on screen; it now points at the panel's own Maximize button, so it cannot come back as a browser window if it is ever switched on. The only thing that still opens a real browser window is the Schwab login, which has to.

releases.heading: The scanner pop-out opens inside the app now, not in a Chrome tab
releases.subheading: Same button, full screen, no browser window
items: Clicking the pop-out button on the MomX scanner used to open a separate browser window - and Chrome was turning that into an ordinary tab, which dropped you out of the app entirely. It now fills the screen with the board inside the app itself. Press the same button again, or Esc, to come back.
It works on the phone too. It was hidden there before, because the old separate-window trick does not work on a phone at all; nothing leaves the page any more, so there is no reason to hide it.

The board behaves exactly as it does in the page - same scrolling in both directions, same pinned toolbar. Measured side by side to be sure. The old pop-out web address still works if you have it saved, and the chart pop-outs are unchanged.

releases.heading: Every scan match now alerts, not just the top 50
releases.subheading: On a busy session more than 50 tickers match - matches 51 and beyond were shown on the board but never pushed to your phone, never got an alert time, and never entered History
items: This morning the Watchlist had 85-99 matches and only 50 were wired to alerts - TSLA, MU, CRWD, IONQ, MARA and about 45 others matched silently. All of them now push, stamp an alert time and archive.
Expect more phone pushes on a busy open. The board still ranks 50 rows at the top; nothing about the scan itself changed.
One bad ticker can no longer knock the whole scan onto its slow single-threaded path.

releases.heading: The phone brief now looks like the one you asked for
releases.subheading: Full brief, one line per line, countdown in the title, nothing cut
items: The notification is the whole brief again - one line per line, in the same order you read it in the app (tape, strongest setup, gainers, losers), with a “Scanner: NFLX” line and the build time underneath. The version from earlier this morning squashed it into one paragraph with “ / ” between the lines and re-sorted them; that was built for a two-line budget that no longer applies.

Nothing is truncated. The catalyst in the brackets - the upgrade, the earnings note, the headline - is the reason the ticker moved, and the old 260-character limit cut every one of them. There is still a safety limit far above any real brief, and if a morning ever did reach it the app drops one catalyst at a time rather than all of them.
The title carries a countdown: “AGX Morning Brief - 13 min to the open”. It also replaces the “- open AGX for the full brief” tail, which had nothing left to point at.

releases.heading: The morning brief on your phone now carries the movers, and waits until it has them
releases.subheading: The 5:30 push was firing before any data existed, and only ever sent the two most useless lines
items: The early push went out on the 5:30 AM build - the emptiest brief of the day, because there are no premarket quotes that early and Schwab publishes no bars before 7:00. So your phone got “No signals yet / Quiet tape so far” and the morning’s push was spent on it. It now waits until the brief actually has something - a scanner signal or a real watchlist mover - and goes out anyway by 7:30 if the morning is genuinely quiet.

The notification only carried the brief’s first two lines, which are always the boilerplate ones (“tape is flat”, “no signals yet”). The movers - the only lines with a ticker and a number - were always the ones cut. On today’s 8:03 brief the old push would have said “tape is flat / no signals” and dropped EOSE +9.9%, DELL +8.4% with its upgrade, MDB -11.7% and CRDO -10.7%. The push now leads with signals and movers, and drops the catalyst text before it drops a whole line.
The 9:00 AM brief is unchanged and still goes out half an hour before the open. What is in the app is unchanged too - this only changes what reaches the phone.

releases.heading: Reloading no longer drops you back to 50 rows
releases.subheading: The saved copy of the board kept all 357 rows but only handed back the top 50 when the app reopened
items: Reload or reopen the app while the scanner is still building a list: you now keep the full list and the right NEWS count instead of the top 50 and a NEWS count that looked too low.
The 'data as of' note also survives a reload again.

releases.heading: NEWS view: the alert time is back on matched tickers
releases.subheading: With NEWS pressed, a ticker that matched the scan shows WHEN IT CAME on the first line and the headline time under it
items: Rows that never matched the scan (on the NEWS view only because they have a headline) still show just the headline time - they have no alert time to show.
Same two-line layout the History tab already uses, so both views read the same way.

releases.heading: Every Watchlist row now carries RVOL, SQZ, Skittles and the rest
releases.subheading: Untick 'Scan matches only' and all 357 rows look like Mag7 rows - no more blank, dimmed lines
items: The scanner used to compute the full set of columns only for its top 50 (thinkorswim's 'Show: 50') and ship the other 307 with just symbol, industry and % change. Now every symbol gets its columns built inside the same parallel workers that already scan it, so the whole list is filled in for about the same cost.
The dimmed rows and the 'top 50 carry every column' note are gone: a row beyond the top 50 renders exactly like one inside it.

News icons now cover the whole list, not just the top 50, and the NEWS button counts and filters over all rows. The headline lookup now follows extra pages when a busy 100-symbol chunk has more than 50 stories in 24 hours, so tickers whose newest story sat below the cut are no longer missed.

What still reads only the top 50 (scan matches first, then biggest movers): the History archive, Momo Alerts and phone pushes, and the live last-price ticking between scans. The rows beyond 50 show the price from the latest scan.

releases.heading: NEWS on the History tab too
releases.subheading: Narrow a day's entries to the ones that had a headline, and combine it with the ticker search
items: History has the same yellow NEWS button as the live board, next to the search box. Press it and only the entries that had news at the time stay - the same rows that carry the newspaper icon. The number on the button is how many entries on the page you are looking at had news.
While NEWS is pressed, each row shows the headline's time in small yellow under the scanner time, e.g. '02:00' with 'Tue 14:13' beneath: the scan saw it at 2:00 AM, the news came Tuesday 2:13 PM.
It works together with the ticker search: type AAPL, press NEWS, and you get AAPL's entries with news across all days.
NEWS narrows the page you are on (400 entries); Newer / Older still walk through the whole archive, and the count line says 'showing 1-400 of 4800 · 37 with news'.
Live board: pressing NEWS now clears any momentum chip or industry chip you had selected, so the NEWS view always starts from the whole board instead of getting stuck behind an earlier filter.

releases.heading: Press NEWS and the Time column shows WHEN each headline came
releases.subheading: Newest headline at the top; 'Tue 17:28 8h' means Tuesday 5:28pm ET, eight hours ago
items: Before: with NEWS pressed the Time column was blank, because it only ever showed when a ticker entered the scan, and most tickers with news never matched. Now, while NEWS is pressed, that column (headed 'News') shows the headline's ET time plus its age, e.g. '00:12 2h'. A headline from an earlier day carries the weekday ('Tue 16:53 9h') so a late-evening stamp cannot be mistaken for tonight.
The NEWS view opens newest-headline-first, and keeps its own order: press NEWS again and the board goes back to exactly the sort you had (High/Low by default).
The Time column shows in the NEWS view even if you have the 'Time' tickbox off; the tickbox itself is left as you set it.
Fixed alongside: clicking the live board's Time header did not actually sort (it looked up a column that was not in its list). It sorts by scan-entry time now.

releases.heading: Untick 'Scan matches only' and you now see all 357, not 50
releases.subheading: The other 307 show industry and % change; the top 50 keep every column
items: Before: the scanner computed the full columns (RVOL, Squeeze, Skittles, chart) for the 50 strongest tickers only and threw the rest away, so unticking 'Scan matches only' showed 50 rows and never the whole list. Now the other 307 arrive too, with industry and % change filled in and the other cells blank - slightly dimmed, with a note under the tickbox saying why.
Computing every column for all 357 would double the scan time, so this is the honest middle: you can scroll or sort the full list and find any ticker, and the heavy columns stay on the top 50.
MATCHES now counts across the whole list, and the Industries roll-up covers all 357 when the tickbox is off.

About the NEWS number: it is how many tickers on the board have a headline - across all 50 the scanner ships, not just the matches you are looking at. Press NEWS and those rows appear; a match without the newspaper icon (like TOST) simply has no headline.

releases.heading: NEWS button next to BULL - see only the scanned tickers that have news
releases.subheading: Press it once to narrow the board, press again to get everything back
items: NEW: a yellow NEWS button beside BULL. The number on it is how many tickers on the board have a headline from the last 24 hours - the same ones that show the little newspaper icon. Press it and the board shows only those rows, with the scan matches still highlighted; press again for the full board.

It looks at the tickers already on the board (the top 50 the scanner ships), not your whole 357-name watchlist, and it ignores 'Scan matches only' on purpose - most nights only a few of the 50 pass the scan and none of them has news, so the NEWS view would have been empty.
It resets to off when you reload, so a filter you forgot about can never make the scan look empty.

releases.heading: Open the scanner in its own window (desktop)
releases.subheading: The pop-out button next to Refresh, like the one MomoX3 has
items: NEW: on a desktop browser the scanner toolbar has a pop-out button (the little box-with-arrow icon). Press it and the scanner opens in a separate window you can drag to a second monitor or park beside your charts. It scans and alerts exactly like the one inside the app.
It only shows on desktop with a mouse - a phone cannot hold two windows side by side, so the button stays hidden there.
Momo Alerts still fire inside the pop-out window.

releases.heading: Add tickers to a list instead of replacing it, and make your own lists
releases.subheading: The Tickers box could only ever REPLACE - that is what wiped your 357 tickers
items: NEW: an Add button in the scanner. Type 'avgo aapl oxy' and press Add (or just Enter) and those tickers join the list. It tells you exactly what happened - 'Added OXY. 357 to 358 tickers' - and says which ones were already there.
Set still exists and still REPLACES the whole list, but it is now the second button, and replacing a big list with a small one asks you to press it twice.
NEW: your own watchlists, like thinkorswim. Tap the list name at the top to switch, rename, delete, or add a new one. Up to 6 - more lists means each one refreshes less often.
The row of tabs is gone. It grew two tabs per list, so six lists filled half a phone screen before any tickers. One list name plus a Live/History switch now, whatever the count.
Adding a ticker to the Watchlist tab stops it following My Watchlist, so it now says so, and Restore reconnects it.
Fixed before you could hit it: Restore on a list you made yourself would have deleted it and then told you it did not exist.
The Find box added last night has been removed.

releases.heading: Release notes are now mandatory
releases.subheading: A commit that changes the app is refused unless this page gets a line
items: Every fix or feature must come with an entry here, in the same commit - a git gate refuses the commit otherwise. Built because the whole of Sep 1 shipped with nothing written, so this page could not answer 'is that fix in yet?'.

releases.heading: Maximize a chart from the grid: scrollbar visible, option column adjustable
releases.subheading: Plus stale chips gone from the MomX strip, and a Restore for the Tickers box
items: Maximizing one chart from the grid (the arrows on the chart's own header) is a different mode from the toolbar's Big screen, and every fix today had gone to Big screen. This one went to the right place: the maximized chart was 12px taller than the window so its bottom scrollbar hid under the taskbar; in a 6-chart grid the drawing rail on the left covered the scrollbar's arrow; and the option column had no divider at all. All three fixed. Drag the thin bar between chart and chain, it is remembered, double-click resets.

MomX momentum strip: removing tickers from a list no longer shows them as LOST (editing the list is not a market event), chips for tickers no longer in the list disappear at once, the strip follows the tab you are on instead of whatever list the scanner last built, and there is a clear button at the end of the strip. The scanner worker needs one restart before the old chips stop coming back.

MomX Tickers box: typing one symbol into it replaced the whole 357-name Watchlist. There is now a Restore button that brings the previous list back, with a two-tap Set/Restore instead of a browser confirm box that never draws on the phone.

releases.heading: Big screen chart mode: divider you can find, width that sticks, nothing off the window
releases.subheading: Five fixes to the toolbar's Big screen view
items: The divider between the big chart and its option chain is visible enough to grab, and the width you drag it to now wins over the default instead of snapping back.
The big-screen workspace no longer runs past the bottom of the window; its height is measured from the frame instead of guessed from the screen size.
Study legends (ADX, MTF clouds, lower studies) were being covered by the floating drawing toolbar, not clipped by the chart - they now sit clear of it.
When the workspace is wider than the window it can scroll sideways instead of cutting off the right-hand panels.

releases.heading: Premarket 'First seen' column, the app installs again, and MomX history paging
releases.subheading: Evening deploy
items: Premarket: a new 'First seen (ET)' column shows when a row actually reached the board, next to the signal's bar time - the two were being confused. A latency log runs through tomorrow's premarket to measure the ~14-minute gap you noticed on AAPL.
Installing AGX as an app from Chrome works again; the install manifest was being fetched without your login and rejected at the door.
MomX history has Newer/Older page buttons at the top and bottom of both history tabs, and the tab bar no longer disappears when a refresh fails while you switch panels.

MomX: the quote trend bars show direction (up vs down) not just size; the script's colour is a rounded pill instead of a full-cell block; the 2H clock, the $3 floor's price source, and the Squeeze sort were corrected.

releases.heading: MomX RVOL matches the TOS script, sector-rotation rows, tidier industry chips
releases.subheading: Afternoon deploy
items: The RVOL column is now the z-score your thinkScript plots, not a plain ratio, and its colours follow the script's ink ladder.
Sector-rotation rows you asked for are on the board.
The industry chips collapse behind a small rectangle toggle so they stop eating the top of the phone screen.
'Within N bars' now means an N-candle window, so a cross lights one bar rather than smearing across several.

releases.heading: Faster MomX: history the phone can render, gzip end to end, quicker Watchlist
releases.subheading: Midday deploy
